title: Measures taken to curb Childhood Hypertension and Obesity
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measures taken to curb Childhood Hypertension and Obesity RBSK 2.0 Expanded to Cover 38 Childhood Health Conditions, Including Diabetes, Hypertension and Mental Health Digital Tracking, Strengthened Mobile Health Teams and IEC Campaign Enhanced Delivery of RBSK 2.0 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 3:53PM by PIB Delhi The Operational Guideliness of RBSK 2.0 of the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) has expanded the programmatic framework to cover 38 common health conditions. The revised guidelines include emerging child health priorities such as non-communicable diseases including diabetes and hypertension, mental health conditions, and behavioural concerns among children. The existing Mobile Health Teams (MHTs) under RBSK are strengthened through additional support of human resources from other existing health programs under National Health Mission for screening in Schools and Anganwadi centres. A comprehensive preventive, promotive, and curative continuum of care approach is used for tracking and follow-up using a digital platform for effective implementation To generate awareness among children and parents regarding lifestyle-related health issues, and to strengthen healthy lifestyle practices Information Education and Communication (IEC) materials like health booklet, videos, and posters have been developed, and shared with States/UTs for dissemination in the community. The Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Smt. Anupriya Patel stated this in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ******* SR HFW/PQ-Measures taken to curb Childhood Hypertension and Obesity/24 July 2026/3 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288846) आगंतुक पटल  : 168 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Measures taken to curb Childhood Hypertension and Obesity RBSK 2.0 Expanded to Cover 38 Childhood Health Conditions, Including Diabetes, Hypertension and Mental Health Digital Tracking, Strengthened Mobile Health Teams and IEC Campaign Enhanced Delivery of RBSK 2.0 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: NHA Convenes BRICS Dialogue on Strengthening Continuum of Care Through Digital Health and Responsible AI
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare NHA Convenes BRICS Dialogue on Strengthening Continuum of Care Through Digital Health and Responsible AI Continuity of Care is the True Measure of Whether Digital Health and AI are Serving Citizens: Union Health Secretary Over 940 million ABHA IDs and 1 billion Linked Digital Health Records Power India's Digital Health Ecosystem: Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava Panel Discusses Digital Public Infrastructure and AI as Key Enablers of Connected, Patient-Centric Healthcare Across BRICS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 3:00PM by PIB Delhi As part of the 16th BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting, a side event titled "From Digital Health Records to AI-Enabled Healthcare: Strengthening the Continuum of Care Through Interoperable Data Infrastructure and Responsible Artificial Intelligence" was organised today, by National Health Authority, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, bringing together policymakers, technical experts and health leaders from BRICS countries to deliberate on the transformative role of digital health infrastructure and responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) in delivering seamless, patient-centric healthcare. The dialogue was anchored in the findings of the BRICS Health Track Technical Working Group 4 (TWG-4) Compendium on Continuum of Care, which underscores the importance of coordinated and uninterrupted health service delivery across different levels of care, healthcare providers and BRICS member states. The Compendium highlights that while continuity of care remains a shared policy objective, its effective implementation is often constrained by the lack of interoperable digital health infrastructure capable of supporting seamless exchange of health information across the patient care journey. In her keynote address, Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava said that the discussions held over the past two days had reflected the collective commitment of BRICS countries to strengthening resilient, equitable and future-ready health systems. She noted that health cooperation remains one of the strongest pillars of the BRICS partnership, founded on mutual learning, shared innovation and a common commitment to achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC). Emphasising that continuity of care lies at the heart of every health system, she said the fundamental challenge before all countries is to ensure that a citizen's healthcare journey—from prevention and diagnosis to treatment, rehabilitation and long-term follow-up—remains connected rather than fragmented across institutions, providers and geographies. She observed that continuity of care is the true measure of whether digital health and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are delivering meaningful benefits to citizens. The Union Health Secretary stated that while no country can build the future of AI-enabled healthcare in isolation, BRICS nations share common challenges, including large and diverse populations, significant rural-urban disparities, a growing burden of chronic and non-communicable diseases, and stretched health workforces. These challenges, she said, make interoperable digital health infrastructure and responsible AI essential tools for strengthening integrated and people-centric healthcare delivery. Highlighting the importance of interoperable digital health records, she said that a person's health journey spans multiple providers and institutions, making it imperative that health information travels securely and seamlessly with the individual. Built on interoperability, open standards and robust governance, digital health records help bridge information gaps between healthcare providers, improve clinical decision-making, reduce duplication of services, strengthen referrals and follow-up, and preserve the continuity of care. Speaking on the role of AI, Smt. Srivastava said that responsible AI is already strengthening healthcare delivery by identifying patients at risk of dropping out of chronic disease management programmes, supporting early interventions, and providing clinical decision support to frontline and community health workers in remote and underserved areas. However, she emphasised that AI is only as effective as the quality of the digital public infrastructure on which it is built, and that trusted, interoperable and citizen-centric digital health systems must remain the foundation of AI-enabled healthcare. Sharing India's experience, the Union Health Secretary highlighted the progress made under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) in creating a federated Digital Public Infrastructure for health. She informed delegates that India has created over 940 million ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) IDs, issued unique digital identities to more than one million healthcare professionals and over five lakh health facilities, while enabling citizens to securely access more than one billion linked digital health records across the continuum of care. She also referred to India's recently launched SAHI (Strategic Framework for AI in Healthcare), unveiled during the AI India Impact Summit earlier this year, which provides a framework for the responsible adoption of AI to strengthen healthcare delivery while ensuring ethics, transparency, safety and citizen trust. The Union Health Secretary emphasised that India's experience was being shared not as a model to be replicated, but as one example among many represented within BRICS. She called for deeper collaboration among member countries on interoperable standards, digital public infrastructure, governance frameworks for responsible AI, cybersecurity, health workforce capacity building, and collaborative research and innovation. Welcoming the release of the BRICS Technical Working Group-4 Compendium on Digital Health Architecture for Continuum of Care, she described it as a significant milestone reflecting the collective expertise and innovation of BRICS nations. She congratulated all member countries and the Technical Working Group for developing the compendium, which demonstrates that despite diverse health systems, BRICS countries are united by a shared vision of connected, equitable and future-ready healthcare. Concluding her address, Smt. Srivastava said that while digital health records provide the foundation, responsible AI offers the opportunity to redefine continuity of care for present and future generations. Speaking at the Occasion, Chief Executive Officer, National Health Authority (NHA), Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal delivered a detailed presentation on the BRICS Technical Working Group-4 (TWG-4) Compendium on Digital Health Architecture for Continuum of Care, outlining its key findings and recommendations. He explained that the compendium provides a comprehensive assessment of the current state of digital health ecosystems across BRICS countries and identifies the critical building blocks required to achieve seamless continuity of care through interoperable digital health infrastructure. Presenting a comparative analysis of the digital health landscape across BRICS nations, Shri Barnwal highlighted the unique strengths and innovations demonstrated by each member country while also identifying the common challenges faced across the grouping. These include fragmented health information systems, limited interoperability, uneven digital maturity across regions, growing burden of chronic and non-communicable diseases, workforce constraints, and the need for robust data governance frameworks. He emphasised that despite the diversity of health systems, BRICS countries share a common aspiration to build connected, patient-centric and resilient healthcare systems. The compendium, he noted, offers a practical framework for strengthening the continuum of care by promoting interoperable digital public infrastructure, adoption of open standards, secure and consent-based data exchange, and the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence. The side event also featured a high-level panel discussion with delegates and experts from BRICS member countries and partner nations, who exchanged experiences and best practices on strengthening the continuum of care through interoperable digital health infrastructure and responsible Artificial Intelligence. The discussion highlighted how countries are leveraging digital public infrastructure to improve continuity of care across diverse healthcare settings. Delegates from Brazil shared their experience with the National Health Data Network (RNDS), which has transformed the country's healthcare ecosystem from paper-based referrals to a unified national health information exchange. They also highlighted the expansion of telehealth services, now reaching nearly 80 per cent of municipalities, significantly improving access to specialist healthcare in remote and underserved regions, including the Amazon. Representatives from Indonesia outlined the rapid scale-up of the country's Integrated Primary Health Care model across thousands of Puskesmas (primary health centres). They also discussed the implementation of the SATUSEHAT digital health platform, which has been adapted to support continuity of care across Indonesia's geographically dispersed archipelago of more than 17,000 islands despite connectivity challenges. The panel underscored that while Artificial Intelligence presents immense opportunities for improving healthcare delivery, its safe and effective deployment depends on high-quality, interoperable health data and locally validated clinical evidence. Participants stressed the need for BRICS countries to invest in robust governance frameworks, data quality, interoperability standards, validation mechanisms, cybersecurity, health workforce capacity building and sustainable financing before scaling AI-enabled healthcare solutions. The dialogue reaffirmed the collective commitment of BRICS countries to harness digital innovation and responsible AI for building resilient, inclusive and people-centric health systems, while advancing universal health coverage and strengthening continuity of care across the health ecosystem. Deputy Minister of Health Vladimir Zelensky, Russia; Mr. Arthur Fernandes da Silva, Brazil; Dr. Hiwot Solomon, Ethiopia; Dr. Harditya Suryawanto, Indonesia; Dr. Grace Achungura, Team lead Health Systems in WHO-India; Ministers, Senior Officers and Delegates from the BRICS member and partner nations participated in the event. ***** SR HFW/16 th BRICS Side Event on AI /24 July 2026/6 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288817) आगंतुक पटल  : 250 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Marathi , Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil Ministry of Health and Family Welfare NHA Convenes BRICS Dialogue on Strengthening Continuum of Care Through Digital Health and Responsible AI Continuity of Care is the True Measure of Whether Digital Health and AI are Serving Citizens: Union Health Secretary Over 940 million ABHA IDs and 1 billion Linked Digital Health Records Power India's Digital Health Ecosystem: Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava Panel Discusses Digital Public Infrastructure and AI as Key Enablers of Connected, Patient-Centric Healthcare Across BRICS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        24 JUL 2026 3:00PM by PIB Delhi As part of the 16th BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting, a side event titled "From Digital Health Records to AI-Enabled Healthcare: Strengthening the Continuum of Care Through Interoperable Data Infrastructure and Responsible Artificial Intelligence" was organised today, by National Health Authority, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, bringing together policymakers, technical experts and health leaders from BRICS countries to deliberate on the transformative role of digital health infrastructure and responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) in delivering seamless, patient-centric healthcare. The dialogue was anchored in the findings of the BRICS Health Track Technical Working Group 4 (TWG-4) Compendium on Continuum of Care, which underscores the importance of coordinated and uninterrupted health service delivery across different levels of care, healthcare providers and BRICS member states. The Compendium highlights that while continuity of care remains a shared policy objective, its effective implementation is often constrained by the lack of interoperable digital health infrastructure capable of supporting seamless exchange of health information across the patient care journey. In her keynote address, Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava said that the discussions held over the past two days had reflected the collective commitment of BRICS countries to strengthening resilient, equitable and future-ready health systems. She noted that health cooperation remains one of the strongest pillars of the BRICS partnership, founded on mutual learning, shared innovation and a common commitment to achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC). Emphasising that continuity of care lies at the heart of every health system, she said the fundamental challenge before all countries is to ensure that a citizen's healthcare journey—from prevention and diagnosis to treatment, rehabilitation and long-term follow-up—remains connected rather than fragmented across institutions, providers and geographies. She observed that continuity of care is the true measure of whether digital health and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are delivering meaningful benefits to citizens. The Union Health Secretary stated that while no country can build the future of AI-enabled healthcare in isolation, BRICS nations share common challenges, including large and diverse populations, significant rural-urban disparities, a growing burden of chronic and non-communicable diseases, and stretched health workforces. These challenges, she said, make interoperable digital health infrastructure and responsible AI essential tools for strengthening integrated and people-centric healthcare delivery. Highlighting the importance of interoperable digital health records, she said that a person's health journey spans multiple providers and institutions, making it imperative that health information travels securely and seamlessly with the individual. Built on interoperability, open standards and robust governance, digital health records help bridge information gaps between healthcare providers, improve clinical decision-making, reduce duplication of services, strengthen referrals and follow-up, and preserve the continuity of care. Speaking on the role of AI, Smt. Srivastava said that responsible AI is already strengthening healthcare delivery by identifying patients at risk of dropping out of chronic disease management programmes, supporting early interventions, and providing clinical decision support to frontline and community health workers in remote and underserved areas. However, she emphasised that AI is only as effective as the quality of the digital public infrastructure on which it is built, and that trusted, interoperable and citizen-centric digital health systems must remain the foundation of AI-enabled healthcare. Sharing India's experience, the Union Health Secretary highlighted the progress made under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) in creating a federated Digital Public Infrastructure for health. She informed delegates that India has created over 940 million ABHA (Ayushman Bharat Health Account) IDs, issued unique digital identities to more than one million healthcare professionals and over five lakh health facilities, while enabling citizens to securely access more than one billion linked digital health records across the continuum of care. She also referred to India's recently launched SAHI (Strategic Framework for AI in Healthcare), unveiled during the AI India Impact Summit earlier this year, which provides a framework for the responsible adoption of AI to strengthen healthcare delivery while ensuring ethics, transparency, safety and citizen trust. The Union Health Secretary emphasised that India's experience was being shared not as a model to be replicated, but as one example among many represented within BRICS. She called for deeper collaboration among member countries on interoperable standards, digital public infrastructure, governance frameworks for responsible AI, cybersecurity, health workforce capacity building, and collaborative research and innovation. Welcoming the release of the BRICS Technical Working Group-4 Compendium on Digital Health Architecture for Continuum of Care, she described it as a significant milestone reflecting the collective expertise and innovation of BRICS nations. She congratulated all member countries and the Technical Working Group for developing the compendium, which demonstrates that despite diverse health systems, BRICS countries are united by a shared vision of connected, equitable and future-ready healthcare. Concluding her address, Smt. Srivastava said that while digital health records provide the foundation, responsible AI offers the opportunity to redefine continuity of care for present and future generations. Speaking at the Occasion, Chief Executive Officer, National Health Authority (NHA), Shri Sunil Kumar Barnwal delivered a detailed presentation on the BRICS Technical Working Group-4 (TWG-4) Compendium on Digital Health Architecture for Continuum of Care, outlining its key findings and recommendations. He explained that the compendium provides a comprehensive assessment of the current state of digital health ecosystems across BRICS countries and identifies the critical building blocks required to achieve seamless continuity of care through interoperable digital health infrastructure. Presenting a comparative analysis of the digital health landscape across BRICS nations, Shri Barnwal highlighted the unique strengths and innovations demonstrated by each member country while also identifying the common challenges faced across the grouping. These include fragmented health information systems, limited interoperability, uneven digital maturity across regions, growing burden of chronic and non-communicable diseases, workforce constraints, and the need for robust data governance frameworks. He emphasised that despite the diversity of health systems, BRICS countries share a common aspiration to build connected, patient-centric and resilient healthcare systems. The compendium, he noted, offers a practical framework for strengthening the continuum of care by promoting interoperable digital public infrastructure, adoption of open standards, secure and consent-based data exchange, and the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence. The side event also featured a high-level panel discussion with delegates and experts from BRICS member countries and partner nations, who exchanged experiences and best practices on strengthening the continuum of care through interoperable digital health infrastructure and responsible Artificial Intelligence. The discussion highlighted how countries are leveraging digital public infrastructure to improve continuity of care across diverse healthcare settings. Delegates from Brazil shared their experience with the National Health Data Network (RNDS), which has transformed the country's healthcare ecosystem from paper-based referrals to a unified national health information exchange. They also highlighted the expansion of telehealth services, now reaching nearly 80 per cent of municipalities, significantly improving access to specialist healthcare in remote and underserved regions, including the Amazon. Representatives from Indonesia outlined the rapid scale-up of the country's Integrated Primary Health Care model across thousands of Puskesmas (primary health centres). They also discussed the implementation of the SATUSEHAT digital health platform, which has been adapted to support continuity of care across Indonesia's geographically dispersed archipelago of more than 17,000 islands despite connectivity challenges. The panel underscored that while Artificial Intelligence presents immense opportunities for improving healthcare delivery, its safe and effective deployment depends on high-quality, interoperable health data and locally validated clinical evidence. Participants stressed the need for BRICS countries to invest in robust governance frameworks, data quality, interoperability standards, validation mechanisms, cybersecurity, health workforce capacity building and sustainable financing before scaling AI-enabled healthcare solutions. The dialogue reaffirmed the collective commitment of BRICS countries to harness digital innovation and responsible AI for building resilient, inclusive and people-centric health systems, while advancing universal health coverage and strengthening continuity of care across the health ecosystem. Deputy Minister of Health Vladimir Zelensky, Russia; Mr. Arthur Fernandes da Silva, Brazil; Dr. Hiwot Solomon, Ethiopia; Dr. Harditya Suryawanto, Indonesia; Dr. Grace Achungura, Team lead Health Systems in WHO-India; Ministers, Senior Officers and Delegates from the BRICS member and partner nations participated in the event. ***** SR HFW/16 th BRICS Side Event on AI /24 July 2026/6 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288817)

title: India Successfully Hosts 3rd BRICS Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Risk Reduction; BRICS Joint Statement Adopted to Advance Global Disaster Resilience
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Home Affairs India Successfully Hosts 3rd BRICS Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Risk Reduction; BRICS Joint Statement Adopted to Advance Global Disaster Resilience प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi Under India's BRICS Chairship 2026, the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, successfully hosted the BRICS Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) in New Delhi on 24 July 2026. The Meeting was chaired by Minister of State for Home Affairs, Shri Nityanand Rai, and attended by Ministers and Heads of Delegation from BRICS Member Countries, reaffirming their shared commitment to strengthening disaster resilience through enhanced cooperation, innovation and sustainable development. The Meeting marked a significant milestone in the evolution of BRICS cooperation on disaster risk reduction and concluded with the unanimous adoption of the BRICS Joint Statement on Disaster Risk Reduction, reaffirming the collective commitment of Member Countries to accelerate implementation of the BRICS Disaster Risk Reduction Work Plan (2025–2028) and deepen cooperation for building resilient societies. Addressing the Ministerial Meeting, Shri Nityanand Rai stated that the evolution of BRICS cooperation—from the Udaipur Declaration (2016) to the Kazan Declaration (2024) and the establishment of the BRICS Disaster Risk Reduction Group (DRRG)—reflects the growing recognition that disaster risk reduction is central to sustainable development, climate resilience and human security. He noted that under India's BRICS Chairship, the Group has adopted a practical and action-oriented approach under the theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability," and appreciated Brazil for elevating the DRR Group to the Ministerial level. Highlighting India's leadership in disaster risk reduction, the Minister said that India's people-centric approach is guided by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Ten-Point Agenda for Disaster Risk Reduction. He emphasized India's five strategic priorities under its Chairship to accelerate implementation of the BRICS DRR Work Plan (2025–2028) and called upon Member Countries to strengthen cooperation in science and technology, early warning systems, resilient infrastructure, nature-based solutions and community resilience to make disaster risk reduction an integral part of sustainable development. The Ministerial Meeting featured a High-Level Policy Dialogue on "Advancing Climate-Smart and Disaster-Resilient Infrastructure Systems: Partnerships, Innovation and Financing for Resilient Development," where Ministers deliberated on resilient infrastructure, innovative financing, emerging technologies and international partnerships to address increasing disaster and climate risks. A Ministerial Roundtable on "Accelerating Implementation of the BRICS Disaster Risk Reduction Work Plan (2025–2028)" enabled Member Countries to exchange experiences and identify practical pathways for strengthening institutional cooperation, capacity building, knowledge sharing and implementation of the agreed priorities. As part of India's Chairship, six flagship knowledge products were launched to support evidence-based policymaking, institutional strengthening, capacity building and practical implementation of disaster risk reduction initiatives across BRICS Member Countries. As a way forward, the Ministers emphasized strengthening practical and action-oriented cooperation through regular technical exchanges, joint projects, simulation exercises, technical expert exchanges and annual thematic workstreams to promote knowledge sharing, innovation and measurable outcomes in disaster resilience. The successful conclusion of the 3rd BRICS Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Risk Reduction reinforces BRICS' collective commitment to advancing resilient, inclusive and sustainable development through strengthened international cooperation on disaster risk reduction. *** RK/PR/PS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288986) आगंतुक पटल  : 223 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Marathi , Gujarati , Telugu Ministry of Home Affairs India Successfully Hosts 3rd BRICS Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Risk Reduction; BRICS Joint Statement Adopted to Advance Global Disaster Resilience प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation hosted the 9th edition of Sujal Gram Samvad
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Jal Shakti Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation hosted the 9th edition of Sujal Gram Samvad Multilingual dialogue held with 8 Gram Panchayats emphasising GP driven community-led Long-Term water security प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, successfully organised the ninth edition of the multilingual ‘Sujal Gram Samvad’ today, reinforcing the government’s commitment to community-led water governance under the Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0. The virtual Samvad witnessed a diverse range of participants including Gram Panchayat (GP) representatives, members of Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), community participants, Jal Sahiyas, Jal Bahinis, Jal Sakhis, Anganwadi workers, students, teachers, and frontline functionaries from the GPs, along with JJM State Mission Directors, District Collectors/District Magistrates/Deputy Commissioners, DWSM officials, and senior officers from the States. The Samvad was chaired by Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS, in the presence of Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM, Shri D Senthil Pandiyan, Joint Secretary, NJJM, along with Senior officers from the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation. In his opening remarks, Secretary, DDWS, Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, emphasised Sujal Gram Samvad as a platform to learn from Gram Panchayat’s experiences and challenges. He said the best practices shared during the interaction can help other Gram Panchayats strengthen their own systems. Shri Ashok K. K Meena underlined that drinking water and sanitation are subjects entrusted to Panchayati Raj Institutions under the 73rd Constitutional Amendment and stressed the need for effective devolution of Funds, Functions and Functionaries (3Fs) to Gram Panchayats for sustainable management of rural water supply systems. He further emphasized that active community ownership through Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), particularly with participation of women, youth and ex-servicemen, is essential for ensuring long-term sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure. Voices from the Gram Panchayats GP- Subbegoundenpudur, District- Coimbatore , Tamil Nadu: During the interaction from representatives of GP Subbegoundenpudur in Tamil , they shared that the GP has achieved 100% Har Ghar Jal coverage across villages and habitations, supplying 55 LPCD through surface water drawn from the Bhavani and Aliyar rivers. Community members highlighted the active involvement of Self-Help Groups in water quality testing through Field Test Kits (FTKs) and regular awareness campaigns on safe water use. The GP collects ₹50 per month i.e ₹600 per annum as user charges. Further, the officials from the District and State informed that the district was declared Har Ghar Jal on 29 th June 2024. They are focusing on strengthening Jal Seva Aankalan, source sustainability measures and standard operating procedures for new household tap connections to ensure sustainable service delivery. A dedicated District Source Sustainability Committee has been constituted to protect drinking water sources and ensure long-term sustainability. Around 80,000 PVTG households have been covered under the Mission. GP- Bariyarpur, District- Lakhisaria, Bihar: The village representatives shared their experiences in Angika language, highlighting water woes prior to JJM and said, many habitations relied on hand pumps and scattered local sources for drinking water. Household tap connections have significantly reduced the burden on women and improved access to safe drinking water. The interaction also highlighted the district's focus on extending piped water supply to remote tribal habitations and strengthening community participation in O&M. District officials informed that surveys have been completed in uncovered tribal hamlets and piped water supply schemes are being implemented in a phased manner. They also highlighted regular DWSM meetings and the gradual transfer of completed schemes to Gram Panchayats for sustainable management. GP- Sonamarg B, District- Ganderbal, Jammu & Kashmir: During the interaction with the village representatives of GP Sonamarg in Hindi , it was informed that the Gram Panchayat receives drinking water through gravity-based spring water supply schemes, which have substantially improved drinking water availability in the mountainous region. They informed that the community actively participates in protection and rejuvenation of natural springs, while youth groups support environmental conservation and cleanliness around tourist areas. The villagers also highlighted that community ownership has strengthened operation and maintenance of the schemes. Being Himalayan region earlier they used to rely on stream water but under JJM even in harsh winter they are getting uninterrupted water because of the insulated pipe water supply technology. District officials informed that the district has undertaken rejuvenation of nearly 30 springs, prepared District Improvement Plans (DIP) for sustainable water security and continues to prioritise source sustainability, gravity-fed systems and convergence with other programmes and local institutions. GP- Lallen, District-Mamit, Mizoram: Interaction with the village members of Mamit was carried out in Mizo language. The beneficiaries reported that the VWSC has established an effective community-led operation and maintenance system. Leakages are reported immediately through WhatsApp groups, while locally engaged plumbers and pump operators attend complaints promptly. Community members highlighted regular awareness campaigns on water conservation and responsible water use. The District Collector informed that DWSM meetings are being held regularly and proceedings are uploaded. Convergence with the Forest Department, Rural Development and Watershed programmes is being strengthened to improve source sustainability, particularly in hilly areas where natural water sources are gradually drying up. GP- Etori, District- Shahjahanpur, Uttar Pradesh: The village representatives shared their experiences in Hindi . Household tap water connections under JJM have significantly improved access to safe drinking water, reducing the drudgery of fetching water and improving the health and well-being of the community. They highlighted that the GP regularly discusses O&M of the water supply system in Gram Sabha meetings, promotes responsible water use and water conservation, and encourages community participation in ensuring the long-term sustainability of the scheme. Village representatives also shared that awareness campaigns are being organised, and the GP is promoting timely reporting and resolution of water supply-related issues. Further District Administration informed that special efforts are being undertaken to provide safe drinking water to Koda and Kora tribal habitations, ensuring that even the most remote and vulnerable communities receive safe drinking water through household tap water connections. They also highlighted regular DWSM meetings, Jan Chaupal programmes for community awareness, and focused orientation of Gram Panchayats on the Jal Sarthi App. GP- Faridpur, District- Panipat, Haryana: The village representatives shared their experiences in Haryanvi language and said that the GP has developed a strong community-led O&M model. A monthly user charge is collected from households and utilised for routine repairs, while locally appointed pump operators and plumbers ensure immediate rectification of leakages and other faults. Monthly ₹13,000 total revenue is collected towards user charge. Self-Help Group women regularly undertake water quality testing through FTKs, while school children, ASHA workers and Anganwadi workers conduct awareness campaigns on water conservation and safe water practices. The GP also uses WhatsApp groups and monthly community meetings for grievance redressal and timely maintenance. District and State officials highlighted Haryana's efforts to implement the State Water Policy by onboarding SHG women for user charge collection, water quality monitoring and grievance redressal, thereby strengthening community ownership of rural water supply schemes. Faridpur GP is the pioneer in implementing the O&M policy. GP- Husir, District- Khunti, Jharkhand: The village representatives shared their experiences in Sadri language and informed that JJM has brought a significant transformation in the predominantly tribal Gram Panchayat by providing household tap water connections, eliminating the need to fetch water from distant streams and improving health. Gram Sabha plays an active role in planning and overseeing the O&M of scheme. A local pump operator has been engaged to ensure regular water supply, while the GP has adopted a community-led user charge mechanism, collecting ₹30 per month per household, with economically weaker families being exempted. The Panchayat collects around ₹9,400 every month, which is utilised for payment of the pump operator, plumber, carrying out routine repairs and addressing pipeline leakages, thereby ensuring uninterrupted water supply and strengthening community ownership of the scheme. District officials informed that a structured monitoring mechanism has been instituted under which district and block-level officers have been assigned villages for regular field visits, with every 4 th Saturday marked for reviewing implementation of JJM and resolving field-level issues. They further shared that the district is working to expand community ownership beyond the VWSC by partnering with Large Area Multi-Purpose Cooperative Societies (LAMPS), Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to strengthen operation and maintenance, user charge collection and long-term sustainability of rural drinking water systems. GP- Kotdhi, District- Balrampur, Chhattisgarh: The village representatives shared their experiences in Hindi and highlighted that JJM has significantly improved access to safe drinking water while reducing the burden of fetching water from distant sources. They informed that drinking water quality is monitored every fortnight using FTKs by trained community members. The test results are promptly shared with villagers through a dedicated WhatsApp group, ensuring transparency and enhancing community awareness regarding water quality. They further shared that soak pits have been constructed for the safe disposal of greywater, contributing to improved sanitation and environmental sustainability. Regular awareness campaigns are also conducted to promote responsible water use and encourage community participation in the maintenance of village water supply assets. The GPs are leveraging 15 th FC grants to support the O&M of rural water supply schemes. District and State officials highlighted the initiatives being undertaken for water conservation through convergence with VB-GRAM G and other programmes. They also shared various local development interventions aimed at strengthening source sustainability and ensuring the long-term sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure. AS & MD, NJJM, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan , expressed appreciation to the active support of District Collectors and Gram Panchayats for their commitment towards JJM. He urged for effective utilisation the 16 th FC grants for which guidelines will be share soon. He emphasised the need for regular DWSM meetings to review the functionality of schemes, address implementation challenges and monitor service delivery. Stressing that source sustainability, he called upon all stakeholders to undertake sustained efforts for protecting and rejuvenating drinking water sources so that future generations continue to receive uninterrupted piped water supply. He further urged District Collectors and District Magistrates to actively participate in Jal Arpan programmes and ensure that all prescribed protocols are followed, thereby promoting community ownership and accountability. Addressing the Gram Pradhans, Shri Soan encouraged them to regularly review the status of their village water supply schemes on the e-Gram Swaraj Portal, use the information for informed decision-making, and proactively share the status with the community through Gram Sabha meetings to strengthen transparency, community participation and collective responsibility for sustainable rural drinking water services. The Samvad started by setting the context and sharing objective by Shri Y K Singh, Director, NJJM. He said that the Samvad aims to listen village communities, understand their experiences and learn local practices on O&M, and source sustenance. *** PS/AK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289090) आगंतुक पटल  : 102 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Jal Shakti Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation hosted the 9th edition of Sujal Gram Samvad Multilingual dialogue held with 8 Gram Panchayats emphasising GP driven community-led Long-Term water security प्रविष्टि तिथि:

They highlighted that the GP regularly discusses O&M of the water supply system in Gram Sabha meetings, promotes responsible water use and water conservation, and encourages community participation in ensuring the long-term sustainability of the scheme. Village representatives also shared that awareness campaigns are being organised, and the GP is promoting timely reporting and resolution of water supply-related issues. Further District Administration informed that special efforts are being undertaken to provide safe drinking water to Koda and Kora tribal habitations, ensuring that even the most remote and vulnerable communities receive safe drinking water through household tap water connections. They also highlighted regular DWSM meetings, Jan Chaupal programmes for community awareness, and focused orientation of Gram Panchayats on the Jal Sarthi App. GP- Faridpur, District- Panipat, Haryana: The village representatives shared their experiences in Haryanvi language and said that the GP has developed a strong community-led O&M model. A monthly user charge is collected from households and utilised for routine repairs, while locally appointed pump operators and plumbers ensure immediate rectification of leakages and other faults. Monthly ₹13,000 total revenue is collected towards user charge. Self-Help Group women regularly undertake water quality testing through FTKs, while school children, ASHA workers and Anganwadi workers conduct awareness campaigns on water conservation and safe water practices. The GP also uses WhatsApp groups and monthly community meetings for grievance redressal and timely maintenance. District and State officials highlighted Haryana's efforts to implement the State Water Policy by onboarding SHG women for user charge collection, water quality monitoring and grievance redressal, thereby strengthening community ownership of rural water supply schemes. Faridpur GP is the pioneer in implementing the O&M policy. GP- Husir, District- Khunti, Jharkhand: The village representatives shared their experiences in Sadri language and informed that JJM has brought a significant transformation in the predominantly tribal Gram Panchayat by providing household tap water connections, eliminating the need to fetch water from distant streams and improving health. Gram Sabha plays an active role in planning and overseeing the O&M of scheme. A local pump operator has been engaged to ensure regular water supply, while the GP has adopted a community-led user charge mechanism, collecting ₹30 per month per household, with economically weaker families being exempted. The Panchayat collects around ₹9,400 every month, which is utilised for payment of the pump operator, plumber, carrying out routine repairs and addressing pipeline leakages, thereby ensuring uninterrupted water supply and strengthening community ownership of the scheme. District officials informed that a structured monitoring mechanism has been instituted under which district and block-level officers have been assigned villages for regular field visits, with every 4 th Saturday marked for reviewing implementation of JJM and resolving field-level issues. They further shared that the district is working to expand community ownership beyond the VWSC by partnering with Large Area Multi-Purpose Cooperative Societies (LAMPS), Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to strengthen operation and maintenance, user charge collection and long-term sustainability of rural drinking water systems. GP- Kotdhi, District- Balrampur, Chhattisgarh: The village representatives shared their experiences in Hindi and highlighted that JJM has significantly improved access to safe drinking water while reducing the burden of fetching water from distant sources. They informed that drinking water quality is monitored every fortnight using FTKs by trained community members. The test results are promptly shared with villagers through a dedicated WhatsApp group, ensuring transparency and enhancing community awareness regarding water quality. They further shared that soak pits have been constructed for the safe disposal of greywater, contributing to improved sanitation and environmental sustainability. Regular awareness campaigns are also conducted to promote responsible water use and encourage community participation in the maintenance of village water supply assets. The GPs are leveraging 15 th FC grants to support the O&M of rural water supply schemes. District and State officials highlighted the initiatives being undertaken for water conservation through convergence with VB-GRAM G and other programmes. They also shared various local development interventions aimed at strengthening source sustainability and ensuring the long-term sustainability of rural drinking water infrastructure. AS & MD, NJJM, Shri Kamal Kishore Soan , expressed appreciation to the active support of District Collectors and Gram Panchayats for their commitment towards JJM. He urged for effective utilisation the 16 th FC grants for which guidelines will be share soon. He emphasised the need for regular DWSM meetings to review the functionality of schemes, address implementation challenges and monitor service delivery. Stressing that source sustainability, he called upon all stakeholders to undertake sustained efforts for protecting and rejuvenating drinking water sources so that future generations continue to receive uninterrupted piped water supply. He further urged District Collectors and District Magistrates to actively participate in Jal Arpan programmes and ensure that all prescribed protocols are followed, thereby promoting community ownership and accountability. Addressing the Gram Pradhans, Shri Soan encouraged them to regularly review the status of their village water supply schemes on the e-Gram Swaraj Portal, use the information for informed decision-making, and proactively share the status with the community through Gram Sabha meetings to strengthen transparency, community participation and collective responsibility for sustainable rural drinking water services. The Samvad started by setting the context and sharing objective by Shri Y K Singh, Director, NJJM. He said that the Samvad aims to listen village communities, understand their experiences and learn local practices on O&M, and source sustenance. *** PS/AK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289090)

title: Government Reiterates Legal Obligations of OTT Platforms and Social Media Under IT Rules, 2021
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Government Reiterates Legal Obligations of OTT Platforms and Social Media Under IT Rules, 2021 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:19PM by PIB Delhi The Government has notified the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 under the Information Technology Act, 2000. PartIII of these Rules provide for publishers of online curated content (OTT platforms) which, inter alia, require the publishers not to transmit any content which is prohibited by law for the time being in force. For the user generated content on intermediary platforms, Part-II of IT Rules, 2021, casts specific due diligence obligations on intermediaries, including social media intermediaries. They should make reasonable efforts by themselves and to cause the users of their computer resource to not display, upload, host, store, transmit, display or publish any such information that is unlawful. This information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to an Unstarred Question in the Rajya Sabha raised by Shri Rajeev Kumar. ***** Mahesh Kumar/ Aparajita Priyadarshini (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288881) आगंतुक पटल  : 252 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Malayalam , Marathi , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Kannada Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Government Reiterates Legal Obligations of OTT Platforms and Social Media Under IT Rules, 2021 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: 386 Private FM Radio Channels Operational; Govt Policy Mandates 20% Content in Local Language to Promote Regional Culture
content:

                24 JUL 2026 3:58PM by PIB Delhi The Government conducted e-auctions for 730 FM channels across 234 new cities on July 9– 10, 2025 through a transparent system. It was widely published in print and electronic media before the auction. During this cycle, there were 18 successful bidders including 9 new entrants to the FM radio sector. There are 386 operational private FM radio channels. Under the Private FM Radio policy, every broadcaster must ensure that at least 20% of its daily broadcast content is in the local language of the city and promotes local content, including programmes on local culture, traditions, and folk music. The Private FM Radio Phase-III policy permits broadcasters to access Prasar Bharati towers and sites, wherever available, for faster rollout. The Government issues Letters of Intent (LOI) and executes Grant of Permission Agreements (GOPA) with clearly defined timelines for operationalisation especially in LWE and aspirational districts. It maintains close coordination with broadcasters for timely dissemination of verified information during emergencies and key campaigns. title: Television Rating Policy, 2026 to Strengthen Transparency, Independence and Accountability in India's TV Audience Measurement System
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Television Rating Policy, 2026 to Strengthen Transparency, Independence and Accountability in India's TV Audience Measurement System New Policy Reduces Net Worth Requirement, Expands Metered Homes and Introduces Periodic Establishment Surveys Policy Mandates Independent Audits, Cross-Holding Restrictions and Graded Penalties to Ensure Credible TV Audience Measurement प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting (MIB) has released the TV Ratings Policy 2026, which sets out comprehensive guidelines for regulating television ratings in India. The policy defines clear standards for the registration, operation, audit, and oversight of agencies providing TV rating services, with the aim of ensuring transparency, independence and accountability in audience measurement. The TV Rating Policy 2026 replaced the existing Guidelines for TV Rating Agencies in India dated 16th January 2014. The major reforms introduced under the Policy include: Reduction of net worth criteria from Rs. 20 Crores to Rs. 5 Crores; Technology-neutral audience measurement across multiple platforms including connected TVs and TV channels available on OTT Platforms; Increased sample size by expansion of metered homes from 50,000 to 80,000; Periodic establishment surveys every three years; Exclusion of landing page in computation of viewership data; Annual independent audits; and A graded penalty framework for non-compliance. The prescribed safeguards include cross-holding restrictions, requirement of at least 33% independent directors on the board of the agency, prohibition of consultancy or advisory activities that may create conflicts of interest, security clearance requirements, audit and transparency obligations to ensure the functional and operational independence of rating agencies. Under this Policy, any entity in the business of television ratings in India has to comply with certain additional requirements and to register under the new Policy. As on date, no entity is registered under the new Policy. The Television Ratings Policy, 2026 places no restriction on the number of agencies that may be registered to provide TV rating services. This information was provided by the Minister of State for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs, Dr. L. Murugan, in a written reply to an Unstarred Question in the Rajya Sabha raised by Dr. John Brittas. **** Mahesh Kumar/ Vivek Vishwash (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288841) आगंतुक पटल  : 401 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali-TR , Assamese , Gujarati , Tamil , Telugu , Kannada Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Television Rating Policy, 2026 to Strengthen Transparency, Independence and Accountability in India's TV Audience Measurement System New Policy Reduces Net Worth Requirement, Expands Metered Homes and Introduces Periodic Establishment Surveys Policy Mandates Independent Audits, Cross-Holding Restrictions and Graded Penalties to Ensure Credible TV Audience Measurement प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Empowering MSME Ecosystem: Advancing Commercial Dispute Resolution through a National ODR Framework
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises Empowering MSME Ecosystem: Advancing Commercial Dispute Resolution through a National ODR Framework Success Stories Reflect the Transformational Impact of MSME Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Portal: From Faster Payments to Stronger MSME प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:27PM by PIB Delhi a) Zeedesign Engineering: Fast-Tracking Payment Recovery through the ODR Portal of Ministry of MSME Mrs. Pragya Verma, Director of Zeedesign Engineering Pvt. Ltd., a Mumbai-based Udyam-registered micro enterprise, successfully recovered ₹21.06 lakh through the MSME Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Portal under the Ministry of MSME's RAMP Programme. Within just 24 hours of filing the petition on the ODR portal, the outstanding payment was released through an amicable settlement, demonstrating the effectiveness of the Ministry's digital dispute resolution mechanism. The success story highlights how the Ministry of MSME is strengthening the financial resilience of micro and small enterprises by ensuring faster payment resolution, promoting Ease of Doing Business and empowering entrepreneurs through transparent and accessible digital governance. b) M/S Shiva Chemicals: Recovering Dues Through the ODR Portal of Ministry of MSME M/S Shiva Chemicals, an Udyam-registered micro enterprise based in Kolkata, West Bengal, faced prolonged payment delays from a public sector buyer despite repeated follow-ups. Finally, the enterprise access the MSME ODR Portal, a digital dispute resolution mechanism and filed its claim before the Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Council (MSEFC) under the MSMED Act, 2006. The intervention led to a mutual settlement, enabling the enterprise to recover ₹4,99,184 against two outstanding invoices. Following the successful resolution, the case was voluntarily withdrawn. This success story highlights how the ODR Portal is enabling faster payment resolution, strengthening the financial resilience of MSME and advancing Ease of Doing Business through transparent and accessible digital justice. MSME Online Dispute Resolution Portal: Fast, Fair and Digital Resolution for MSME Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) are the backbone of India's economy, driving entrepreneurship, creating jobs and contributing to inclusive growth. Recognising the need for a faster and more efficient way to resolve commercial disputes, the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises has launched the MSME Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) Portal . The Portal provides a simple, transparent and cost-effective digital platform for resolving commercial disputes, particularly delayed payment issues. By reducing dependence on lengthy litigation, it enables quicker settlements, helps businesses maintain healthy cash flows and strengthens trust between buyers and suppliers. In addition to serving as a dispute resolution platform, the MSME ODR Portal encourages dialogue and collaboration. It helps businesses settle disputes amicably through negotiation, mediation and mutual agreement, preserving long-term commercial relationships and allowing entrepreneurs to focus on growing their businesses instead of pursuing prolonged legal proceedings. Resolve Disputes Before They Escalate One of the Portal's key features is its pre-MSEFC negotiation mechanism . Before a dispute reaches the MSEFC, buyers and suppliers are given an opportunity to engage with each other through a structured digital platform. The Portal allows both parties to communicate their concerns, exchange relevant information and work towards a mutually acceptable solution in a non-adversarial environment. This approach saves time, reduces costs and helps maintain business relationships. To support informed decision-making, the Portal also offers a Digital Guided Pathway that analyses the dispute and provides an indication of its likely outcome. This gives both parties greater clarity about their position and encourages realistic, informed settlements. When disputes are resolved at this stage, businesses receive quicker outcomes while MSEFCs are able to devote more time to complex cases requiring formal intervention. Accessible by Every MSME The MSME ODR Portal has been designed to ensure that dispute resolution is accessible by every micro and small enterprise, regardless of location or digital familiarity. With an intuitive interface, simplified workflows and support for vernacular languages, entrepreneurs can easily initiate negotiations and participate in the resolution process from anywhere. Where disputes require formal intervention, the Portal enables online conciliation and arbitration before the MSEFC, eliminating geographical barriers and reducing procedural delays. By making dispute resolution digital, accessible and transparent, the MSME ODR Portal supports the Government's vision of Digital India, Ease of Doing Business and an inclusive MSME ecosystem where every enterprise has equitable access to justice. title: Meeting of Consultative Committee for the Ministry of Power Held
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Power Meeting of Consultative Committee for the Ministry of Power Held Committee discusses consumer-centric framework for parallel distribution licensing प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 5:24PM by PIB Delhi The Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Power met yesterday under the chairmanship of Union Minister for Power and Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Manohar Lal, to deliberate on the proposed framework for parallel distribution licensing aimed at promoting consumer choice, improving service quality and ensuring efficient utilisation of electricity distribution infrastructure. The meeting was attended by Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for Power, Members of Parliament w ho are members of the Consultative Committee , Secretary, Ministry of Power and senior officials of Ministry of Power. Addressing the Committee, the Union Minister stated that the Electricity Act, 2003 had successfully introduced competition in electricity generation, transmission and trading, while distribution remains the only major segment where competition continues to be limited. He emphasised that as India moves towards becoming a developed nation under the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 , consumers will increasingly expect reliable, affordable and high-quality electricity supply comparable to global standards. It was discussed that while the existing legal framework permits more than one distribution licensee in the same area, it requires each licensee to establish its own distribution network. This results in duplication of poles, lines and substations, increases capital expenditure and discourages fresh investment, ultimately leading to inefficient utilisation of resources. The proposed framework seeking to enable competition in electricity supply without requiring duplication of the physical distribution network was discussed in detail. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks. New distribution licensees will be able to use the existing network by paying regulated wheeling charges, while retaining the option to develop their own network wherever permitted by the concerned State Electricity Regulatory Commission. The Minister highlighted that the detailed implementation framework would be developed by the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions to ensure fairness, transparency and non-discriminatory access to the network. The proposal also fully protects the interests of incumbent distribution licensees and their employees. Further, all distribution licensees will continue to be bound by the universal service obligation under the Electricity Act, and the regulatory framework will prevent selective supply only to profitable consumers. Emphasising the consumer-centric nature of the reform, Shri Manohar Lal stated that consumers would have the freedom to choose their electricity supplier, similar to the choices available today in sectors such as telecommunications and aviation. Increased competition is expected to encourage better consumer service, improved reliability, greater innovation and operational efficiency, while ensuring optimal utilisation of existing infrastructure and avoiding unnecessary expenditure. The Minister noted that the concept is not new to India and has been successfully implemented in Mumbai for several years, where consumers have exercised supplier choice while the distribution network continues to be developed in a coordinated manner under the supervision of the State Electricity Regulatory Commission. The members of Parliament participated actively in the discussions and offered valuable suggestions on various aspects of the proposed framework. Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for Power thanked the Members for their constructive inputs and reaffirmed the Government's commitment to carrying forward reforms that place consumers at the centre of India's power sector while ensuring efficiency, transparency and sustainable growth. *** NR/MD (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288973) आगंतुक पटल  : 152 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Power Meeting of Consultative Committee for the Ministry of Power Held Committee discusses consumer-centric framework for parallel distribution licensing प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Dedicated Environment & Housekeeping Management Departments Established at Divisions, Zonal Railways and Railway Board to Monitor and Handle Waste Management Related Matters: Railway Minister
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Railways Dedicated Environment & Housekeeping Management Departments Established at Divisions, Zonal Railways and Railway Board to Monitor and Handle Waste Management Related Matters: Railway Minister On Board Housekeeping Service Available in 1,450 pairs of Long-distance Trains to Ensure end-to-end Cleanliness and Hygiene Clean Train Station Scheme Implemented at 63 Stations Covering 2,800 Trains, Ensuring Cleaner Coaches, Improved Hygiene and Enhanced Passenger Convenience Indian Railways Commissioned 13 Bio-gas Plants, 171 Composting Plants and 8 Material Recovery Facilities at Stations to Promote Scientific Waste Processing and Environmentally Sustainable Waste Management प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:37PM by PIB Delhi Indian Railways has adopted a comprehensive mechanism for collection, treatment and disposal of waste generated from trains and railway stations. At stations, twin dustbins have been provided for collection and segregation of waste at source.  Waste generated in the trains is collected at regular intervals at nominated waste handling stations. These stations have tie-ups with Urban Local Bodies/Municipal Authorities for proper disposal of waste. Further, Indian Railways has also established Waste processing plants as Bio-gas, Composting and Plastic Bottle Crushing Machines at different stations based on operational needs. Details of such facilities are as below: S.No. Type of Plant No. of Plants commissioned Installed Capacity 1 Bio-gas plant 13 5,095 kg per day 2 Composting Plant 171 24,817 kg per day 3 Material Recovery Facility 08 7,725 kg per day 4 Plastic Bottle Crushing Machines 858 machines Pursuant to the applicability of new Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 and directions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, Indian Railways has initiated a series of measures for strengthening solid waste management across its establishments. The Railway Board has issued Standard Operating Procedure (SoP) on Solid Waste Management covering railway stations, trains, railway colonies, hospitals, workshops, production units and all other railway establishments. SoP provides detailed guidelines regarding segregation, collection, transportation, processing and scientific disposal of waste, monitoring mechanisms and well defined responsibilities at all administrative levels. Zonal Railways has initiated identification of its units which qualify as bulk waste generators as per SWM Rules, 2026. An “As-is Waste Characterization and Quantification Study” has been planned to assess the existing waste generation across all Indian Railways establishments and trains. Zonal Railways have also nominated dedicated Nodal Officers to prepare comprehensive action plans for Waste Management, conduct periodic audits, monitor implementation and regularly share compliance reports to Railway Board. Divisions have also been directed to prepare action plans for effective waste management. Dedicated Environment & Housekeeping Management (EnHM) departments have been established at Divisions, Zonal Railways and Railway Board level to monitor and handle waste management related matters. To ensure effective end-to-end cleanliness and hygiene management in trains, On board housekeeping service (OBHS) is provided which is currently available in 1450 (pairs) identified long distance trains. The Clean Train Station (CTS) scheme at 63 stations has been implemented covering 2800 trains. Under this scheme, a dedicated team of staff equipped with cleaning equipment carries out cleaning of coach toilets & washbasins and collects garbage from train’s dustbins during halt time. This information was provided by the Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, in a reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288897) आगंतुक पटल  : 169 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Kannada Ministry of Railways Dedicated Environment & Housekeeping Management Departments Established at Divisions, Zonal Railways and Railway Board to Monitor and Handle Waste Management Related Matters: Railway Minister On Board Housekeeping Service Available in 1,450 pairs of Long-distance Trains to Ensure end-to-end Cleanliness and Hygiene Clean Train Station Scheme Implemented at 63 Stations Covering 2,800 Trains, Ensuring Cleaner Coaches, Improved Hygiene and Enhanced Passenger Convenience Indian Railways Commissioned 13 Bio-gas Plants, 171 Composting Plants and 8 Material Recovery Facilities at Stations to Promote Scientific Waste Processing and Environmentally Sustainable Waste Management प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Indian Railways Initiates AI-based Stain Detection Pilot Project in Laundries at Pune, Jaipur & Jodhpur Divisions to Enhance Quality of Washed Linen
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Initiates AI-based Stain Detection Pilot Project in Laundries at Pune, Jaipur & Jodhpur Divisions to Enhance Quality of Washed Linen Whito-Meters Used in All Mechanised Laundries to Ensure Effective Linen Cleaning; CCTV Cameras Installed Across Laundries for Continuous Monitoring of Laundry Operations प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi Indian Railways (IR) provides clean and hygienic linen to passengers travelling in AC classes in each trip. Each bedroll packet contains two bed sheets, one pillow cover and a hand towel. One bed sheet is intended for keeping it on sleeper seat while the additional bed sheet provided in the standard bedroll kit is intended as a covering layer under blanket so that blanket is not in direct touch with the body of passenger.  This blanket cover sheet is washed after single use. As a pilot initiative to enhance passenger experience, blanket covers are being provided to all AC class passengers in trains operated by North Western Railway and in newly launched Vande Bharat Sleeper Train operating between Kamakhya and Howrah.  This initiative has been widely appreciated by the passengers. Whito-Meters are used in all mechanised laundries to check the effectiveness of cleaning of linen. CCTV cameras have been installed across laundries over IR to monitor laundry operations. Indian Railways has also initiated the pilot project of using automated AI-camera stain detection technology in laundries at Pune Division, Central Railway and Jaipur & Jodhpur division, North Western Railway for ascertaining the quality of washed linen. The Codal life of various linen items is prescribed under the extant Railway rules and is reviewed periodically based on usage, condition and serviceability. Linen items found unserviceable are withdrawn and replaced in accordance with the prescribed norms. The prescribed service life of various constituents of the linen kit is as under: S. No. Item Codal Life 1 Bed sheet (a) 12 months for Handloom linen (b) 24 months for Polyvastra supplied by KVIC 2 Pillow cover 9 months 3 Face Towel 9 months 4 Pillow 24 months 5 Woollen Blanket 24 months This information was provided by the Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, in a reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288887) आगंतुक पटल  : 173 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Kannada Ministry of Railways Indian Railways Initiates AI-based Stain Detection Pilot Project in Laundries at Pune, Jaipur & Jodhpur Divisions to Enhance Quality of Washed Linen Whito-Meters Used in All Mechanised Laundries to Ensure Effective Linen Cleaning; CCTV Cameras Installed Across Laundries for Continuous Monitoring of Laundry Operations प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: CCTV Surveillance Systems Provided at 3,215 Railway Stations and 13,409 Passenger Coaches to Strengthen Passenger Safety and Security
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Railways CCTV Surveillance Systems Provided at 3,215 Railway Stations and 13,409 Passenger Coaches to Strengthen Passenger Safety and Security Northern Railway Leads with CCTV Coverage at 425 Stations, followed by Western Railway (391) and Eastern Railway (271) Western Railway Tops in CCTV-equipped Passenger Coaches with 1,735 Coaches, followed by Northern Railway (1,483) and Southern Railway (1,481) All Operational Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat Train Rakes Equipped with CCTV Cameras प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:17PM by PIB Delhi Installation of CCTV surveillance systems at railway stations, passenger coaches and other railway premises has been planned across the Indian Railways network with the objective of strengthening passenger safety and enhancing security surveillance. The installation of CCTV surveillance systems is being undertaken in a phased manner. All operational Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat train rakes have already been equipped with CCTV cameras. So far, CCTV surveillance systems have been provided at 3,215 railway stations and 13,409 passenger coaches. The zone-wise details are as follows: S.No Railway Zone Number of stations provided with CCTV system Number of coaches fitted with cameras 1. Central Railway 240 1384 2. Eastern Railway 271 1288 3. The installed CCTV cameras at stations are equipped with AI-based video analytics features, such as intrusion detection, loitering detection and fallen person detection. title: Cabinet approves one multitracking project covering three Districts across Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, increasing the existing network of Indian Railways by about 46 Kms
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Railways Cabinet approves one multitracking project covering three Districts across Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, increasing the existing network of Indian Railways by about 46 Kms The total estimated cost of the project is Rs 1,264 crore and will be completed up to 2028-29. प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:06PM by PIB Delhi The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today has approved 3 rd and 4 th Line of Ballari – Guntakal section in Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh with total cost of Rs. 1,264 crore (approx.). The project is planned on PM-Gati Shakti National Master Plan with focus on enhancing multi-modal connectivity & logistic efficiency through integrated planning and stakeholder consultations. This project will provide seamless connectivity for movement of people, goods, and services. The project covering 03 Districts across the states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh will increase the existing network of Indian Railways by about 46 Kms. The proposed multi-tracking project will enhance connectivity to approximately 99 villages, which are having a population of about seven lakhs. The capacity enhancement will improve rail connectivity to several prominent tourist destinations across the country, including Ballari Fort, Sri Kumara Swamy Temple, etc. The proposed project is essential route for transportation of commodities such as iron ore, dolomite, limestone, iron and steel, coal, fertilizers, food grains, etc. The capacity augmentation works will result in additional freight traffic of magnitude 16.22 MTPA (Million Tonnes Per Annum). The Railways being environment friendly and energy efficient mode of transportation, will help both in achieving climate goals and minimizing logistics cost of the country, reduce oil import (1.32 Crore Litres) and lower CO2 emissions (6.67 Crore Kg) which is equivalent to plantation of 0.27 crore trees. The increased line capacity will significantly enhance mobility, resulting in improved operational efficiency and service reliability for Indian Railways. This multi-tracking proposal is poised to streamline operations and alleviate congestion. The project is in line with the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modiji’s Vision of a New India which will make people of the region “Atmanirbhar” by way of comprehensive development in the area which will enhance their employment/ self-employment opportunities. *** MJPS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288860) आगंतुक पटल  : 221 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Punjabi , Gujarati , Kannada , Malayalam Ministry of Railways Cabinet approves one multitracking project covering three Districts across Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, increasing the existing network of Indian Railways by about 46 Kms The total estimated cost of the project is Rs 1,264 crore and will be completed up to 2028-29. प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PROGRESS UNDER DDU-GKY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development PROGRESS UNDER DDU-GKY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi DDU-GKY is one of the cluster of initiatives under Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) aimed at livelihood diversification and poverty reduction. DDU-GKY aims to skill rural youth and promote sustainable livelihoods for rural youth through placement linked skilling programs. Under DDU-GKY, efforts are made to align the aspirations of rural youth with the evolving skill requirements of the labour market. States/UTs are provided budgetary support to undertake skill gap studies to identify sectoral opportunities and employment potential in their regions. Based on these studies, States/UTs and Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) are encouraged to propose training programmes in emerging and high-growth sectors aligned with local, domestic and global job markets. While submitting project proposals, PIAs are required to provide justification and demand assessment for the sectors proposed, ensuring that training under DDU-GKY remains demand-driven and industry-relevant. So far under DDUGKY, a total of 18.45 lakh candidates has been trained and 12.35 lakh have been placed till June 2026. The sectors that have been identified for the training and placement of rural youth under the said scheme are given as Annexure I . Funds are released to Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs), subject to achieving the placement target. PIAs are required to ensure placement of at least 70% of trained candidates, with at least 50% placed in wage employment. Post Placement Support (PPS) is provided to eligible candidates to facilitate retention for a period of six months and tracking for up to twelve months. The Budget Estimate (BE) for the FY 2026-27 is ₹ 750.00 crore as Central Share. This information was given by Minister of State for the Rural Development , Shri Kamlesh Paswan in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.
