title: STATUS OF IMPLEMENTATION OF PMGSY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development STATUS OF IMPLEMENTATION OF PMGSY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 5:45PM by PIB Delhi Under the various ongoing verticals of the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), a total of 2,905 roads covering 15,647.78 km and 1,042 bridges were completed across the country during the financial year 2025–26. In addition, 93 eligible habitations were provided with all-weather road connectivity. Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana-I (PMGSY-I) was launched as a one-time special intervention to provide rural connectivity, by way of a single all-weather road, to the eligible unconnected habitations in the core network for uplifting the socio-economic condition of the rural population. Under this scheme 1,62,876 habitations were provided connectivity. This scheme was closed on 31.03.2025 and no new further sanction was issued. However, timeline extension was given up to 31.03.2027 to complete any of the balance works and payments. Subsequently, new intervention/verticals namely PMGSY-II for up-gradation of 50,000 Km of the existing rural roads and PMGSY-III for consolidation of 1, 25,000 Km Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting habitations, inter-alia , to Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs), Higher Secondary Schools and Hospitals, were added under the ambit of PMGSY. PMGSY II and III are schemes to provide all weather connectivity to habitations and connectivity to government institutions. Since September 2024, PMGSY-IV has been launched with an objective to provide connectivity to 25000 unconnected habitations by the year 2029. State/UT wise details may be accessed at home page of programme website https://pmgsy.dord.gov.in >habitations coverage. (b) & (c): The implementation plan for PMGSY during the Financial Year 2026–27 focuses on the timely completion of ongoing works and up-gradation of rural roads and strengthening the maintenance of the already constructed roads. The key components of the implementation plan are as follows: (i)  Expeditious completion of ongoing works sanctioned under the various verticals of PMGSY (except PMGSY II which has been closed since 31.03.2026). (ii)  Sanction of rural roads projects under PMGSY-IV, in accordance with the approved framework and scheme guidelines, to provide all weather connectivity to unconnected habitations. (iii)  Maintenance of PMGSY roads by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations in accordance with the programme guidelines. (iv)  Strengthening digital maintenance management through the Electronic Maintenance of Rural Roads (eMARG) platform for planning, inspections, performance-based payments and monitoring of maintenance works. (v)  Quality assurance through the three-tier quality monitoring mechanism comprising Programme Implementation Units (PIUs), State Quality Monitors (SQMs) and National Quality Monitors (NQMs), and supplemented by geo-tagged inspections. (vi)  Regular monitoring and capacity building through review meetings, Regional Review Meetings (RRMs), field inspections and advisories to ensure timely implementation, quality construction and sustainable maintenance of rural road assets. These measures are aimed at achieving the annual physical targets for FY 2026–27 while ensuring durable, high-quality rural road infrastructure and improved connectivity across the country. Accordingly, a target has been fixed for the completion of 26,474 km of rural roads, 1,375 bridges and connectivity to 2,400 eligible habitations, during FY 2026–27, under the various verticals of PMGSY, including PMGSY-I, PMGSY-III, Road Connectivity Project for Left Wing Extremism Affected Areas (RCPLWEA), PM-JANMAN and PMGSY-IV (given at Annexure-I ). Under PMGSY, special emphasis is accorded to improving rural road connectivity in Aspirational Districts, tribal areas, Left Wing Extremism (LWE)-affected areas and other remote and difficult regions, in accordance with the scheme guidelines and approved framework. title: SHGS FORMED UNDER DAY-NRLM
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development SHGS FORMED UNDER DAY-NRLM प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi Under Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), 92 lakh Self Help Groups (SHGs) have been formed across the country, covering 10.05 crore rural women. Under DAY-NRLM, the Ministry is promoting financial inclusion of women Self Help Group (SHG) members through financial literacy, enhanced access to institutional credit, and promotion of micro-enterprises. To deepen financial inclusion in rural areas, particularly among women SHG members, DAY-NRLM has launched a comprehensive Financial Literacy Programme in partnership with Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) and banks. Financial Literacy Community Resource Persons conduct village-level financial literacy camps covering modules on Financial Planning, Savings, Credit, Insurance, Pension, Enterprise Financing, and Business Correspondence. During the Financial Year 2025–26, more than 3.81 crore women SHG members were imparted financial literacy training on these modules. Further, all Public Sector Banks and one private sector bank have designed their own dedicated credit products for individual women SHG members under DAY-NRLM to facilitate the Lakhpati Didi initiative. These credit products enable women SHG members to establish new enterprises or expand their existing enterprises by availing institutional credit at affordable rates. title: EMPLOYMENT GENERATION UNDER VB-G RAM G SCHEME
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development EMPLOYMENT GENERATION UNDER VB-G RAM G SCHEME प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 5:41PM by PIB Delhi The Government continuously reviews the implementation of the programme in consultation with the States/UTs and takes appropriate measures to address implementation-related issues. Under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, employment was provided to all rural households that demanded work, in accordance with the provisions of the Act. The number of person-days generated varied across States/UTs and financial years depending upon the demand for employment registered by rural households. The year-wise and States/Union Territories-wise details of persondays generated under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS during the last five financial years is given at Annexure. For Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Act, which has been operationalized with effect from 01.07.2026 a comprehensive online Management Information System (MIS) has been put in place for real time monitoring of implementation and addressing the issues if any faced by implementing agencies. Further, Ministry has deputed large number of officers to the States to review its implementation and provide handholding support to States. To ensure timely wage payments, the Ministry has implemented the National Electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS) and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), under which wages are directly credited into the bank accounts of beneficiaries. The Ministry has also issued detailed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) prescribing timelines and responsibilities at various levels for timely processing of wage payments. Further, technology-enabled Management Information Systems (MIS) are used for real-time monitoring and tracking of wage payments, pendency at different stages, and regular review with the States/UTs to facilitate timely resolution of issues. In addition, the Ministry regularly releases funds to the States/UTs based on the actual demand from ground and fulfilment of statutory and financial requirements, to ensure smooth implementation of the programme. The Government has enacted the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025, which has come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026 across all rural areas of the country. The Act strengthens the rural employment guarantee framework by enhancing the statutory employment guarantee from 100 days to 125 days per rural household in a financial year. The Government has made adequate budgetary provision for effective implementation of the programme. For the financial year 2026–27, a Central share of ₹95,692.31 crore has been provided for the Scheme, representing the highest-ever Budget Estimate for rural employment. With the corresponding estimated State share, the total programme outlay is expected to exceed ₹1.51 lakh crore. To ensure timely wage disbursal, the Ministry has implemented the National Electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS) and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), and established technology-enabled Management Information Systems (MIS) for real-time monitoring and review of wage payments. The Act accords high priority to Livelihood-related Infrastructure as one of its core thematic areas and adopts a Whole-of-Government Approach through convergence with agriculture, allied sectors and other Government programmes. It permits the creation of rural infrastructure such as Skill Development Centres, Rural Libraries, Digital Learning Centres and other community assets that promote skilling, learning and sustainable livelihoods.                         24 JUL 2026 5:41PM by PIB Delhi The Government continuously reviews the implementation of the programme in consultation with the States/UTs and takes appropriate measures to address implementation-related issues. Under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS, employment was provided to all rural households that demanded work, in accordance with the provisions of the Act. The number of person-days generated varied across States/UTs and financial years depending upon the demand for employment registered by rural households. The year-wise and States/Union Territories-wise details of persondays generated under Mahatma Gandhi NREGS during the last five financial years is given at Annexure. For Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB–G RAM G) Act, which has been operationalized with effect from 01.07.2026 a comprehensive online Management Information System (MIS) has been put in place for real time monitoring of implementation and addressing the issues if any faced by implementing agencies. Further, Ministry has deputed large number of officers to the States to review its implementation and provide handholding support to States. To ensure timely wage payments, the Ministry has implemented the National Electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS) and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), under which wages are directly credited into the bank accounts of beneficiaries. The Ministry has also issued detailed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) prescribing timelines and responsibilities at various levels for timely processing of wage payments. Further, technology-enabled Management Information Systems (MIS) are used for real-time monitoring and tracking of wage payments, pendency at different stages, and regular review with the States/UTs to facilitate timely resolution of issues. In addition, the Ministry regularly releases funds to the States/UTs based on the actual demand from ground and fulfilment of statutory and financial requirements, to ensure smooth implementation of the programme. The Government has enacted the Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB–G RAM G Act, 2025, which has come into force with effect from 1st July, 2026 across all rural areas of the country. The Act strengthens the rural employment guarantee framework by enhancing the statutory employment guarantee from 100 days to 125 days per rural household in a financial year. The Government has made adequate budgetary provision for effective implementation of the programme. For the financial year 2026–27, a Central share of ₹95,692.31 crore has been provided for the Scheme, representing the highest-ever Budget Estimate for rural employment. With the corresponding estimated State share, the total programme outlay is expected to exceed ₹1.51 lakh crore. To ensure timely wage disbursal, the Ministry has implemented the National Electronic Fund Management System (NeFMS) and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), and established technology-enabled Management Information Systems (MIS) for real-time monitoring and review of wage payments. The Act accords high priority to Livelihood-related Infrastructure as one of its core thematic areas and adopts a Whole-of-Government Approach through convergence with agriculture, allied sectors and other Government programmes. It permits the creation of rural infrastructure such as Skill Development Centres, Rural Libraries, Digital Learning Centres and other community assets that promote skilling, learning and sustainable livelihoods. title: DEPARTMENT OF LAND RESOURCES CLARIFIES FACTS ON 'NAKSHA' PILOT PROJECT IN GOA; CONFIRMS ORIGINAL LAND RECORDS REMAIN FULLY PROTECTED
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Rural Development DEPARTMENT OF LAND RESOURCES CLARIFIES FACTS ON 'NAKSHA' PILOT PROJECT IN GOA; CONFIRMS ORIGINAL LAND RECORDS REMAIN FULLY PROTECTED A Digital Shield for Margao: How the NAKSHA Project is Securing Our Property Rights प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:40PM by PIB Delhi There is fantastic news for property owners in Margao and Cuncolim and Panaji city as the Department of Land Resources’ flagship urban mapping pilot, NAKSHA, transitions into its next crucial phase. Despite misleading rumours attempting to cause panic over property boundaries and land titles, the verified facts show that this initiative is one of the most citizen-friendly digital governance programs introduced under the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP). By bringing pinpoint accuracy to urban mapping, NAKSHA is set to eliminate boundary confusion and provide long-term security to local landowners. The greatest benefit of this modern GIS and drone-based mapping system is its ability to protect citizens from future boundary friction. By physically verifying electronic maps against actual field conditions—a process known as ground-truthing—the project ensures that your actual land boundaries match the official records perfectly. This drastically reduces the likelihood of future disputes, bringing peace of mind to common citizens and ensuring that local municipal bodies can plan top-tier public utilities and infrastructure directly serving our neighbourhoods. The program features built-in public verification cycles specifically designed to protect absent owners, ensuring that a physical absence during the survey has no impact on legal ownership. The formal inquiry process will open from July 16 to August 14, 2026, at the Office of the Inspector of Survey and Land Records (ISLR) in the Osia Commercial Arcade, SGPDA Market, Margao. This is an excellent opportunity for the community to bring their title documents forward and map them accurately into the digital age. You don't need any technical knowledge, as helpful survey officials will assist you step-by-step. Let’s reject the rumors, embrace transparency, and work together to make Goa’s urban spaces secure for generations to come. ***** RC/HR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288902) आगंतुक पटल  : 119 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी Ministry of Rural Development DEPARTMENT OF LAND RESOURCES CLARIFIES FACTS ON 'NAKSHA' PILOT PROJECT IN GOA; CONFIRMS ORIGINAL LAND RECORDS REMAIN FULLY PROTECTED A Digital Shield for Margao: How the NAKSHA Project is Securing Our Property Rights प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Two Days of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 successfully concluded at IIT Hyderabad with focus on AI for Sustainability and Global South Cooperation
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology Two Days of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 successfully concluded at IIT Hyderabad with focus on AI for Sustainability and Global South Cooperation प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 7:32PM by PIB Delhi The Day 01 of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 with the focal theme “Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development and Strengthening Global South Cooperation” commenced today at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Hyderabad , bringing together member and participating countries from BRICS to deliberate on the 3C’s Collective, Collaborative and Context sensitive approaches towards Artificial Intelligence (AI). The forum witnessed the presence of 08 BRICS member countries - Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Russia and South Africa along with 05 BRICS partner countries - Nigeria, Vietnam, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Malaysia. Delivering the Presidential Address of the host academy - Indian National Science Academy (INSA), Prof. Shekhar Mande , President of INSA, underscored the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing priority global and global south challenges, and also emphasized the importance of ensuring that AI systems remain ethical, inclusive, transparent and accessible to all socio-economic fabric of the society. Dr. Debashis Mitra , Vice President (International Affairs), INSA delivered the context-setting address, underlining the urgency for strengthened multilateral scientific engagement. This was followed by an institutional address by Prof. B. S. Murty , Director of IIT Hyderabad who focussed on the various AI associated programmes undertaken at IIT Hyderabad. Key Focus Areas of AI Collaboration The deliberations identified five priority verticals for AI-driven interventions: Advanced Materials and Manufacturing: Accelerating materials discovery, enabling smart manufacturing and optimizing supply chains. Healthcare: Enhancing clinical decision-making, enabling population-scale screening and advancing health research. Climate Change and Environmental Sustainability: Improving long-term forecasting, integrating AI with physical models and enabling risk mitigation. Agriculture and Food Security: Providing AI-powered advisories, accelerating seed research and leveraging digital public infrastructure. Disaster Prediction and Management: Strengthening forecasting capabilities, seismic analysis and resource optimization during emergencies. The thematic focus of the Forum was introduced in the Statement Overview session led by Prof. Ambuj Sagar , IIT Delhi and set the stage for detailed deliberations. Representatives from participating academies presented their national perspectives and engaged in substantive discussions. Brazilian Academy of Sciences emphasized inclusive AI for healthcare, climate resilience and food security Chinese Academy of Sciences highlighted data sharing, validation  and evidence-based policymaking aligned with SDGs. Academy of Scientific Research and Technology, Egypt called for capacity building and a BRICS AI Network Ethiopian Academy of Sciences stressed preservation of linguistic diversity alongside cybersecurity and AI education. Indonesian Academy of Sciences underlined explainability, ethical risks and the need for AI to augment human judgement. Russian Academy of Sciences advocated trusted AI systems with strong ethics, transparency and institutional mechanisms such as Centres of Excellence. Academy of Science of South Africa focused on addressing the digital divide and prioritizing climate, health and food security. The Nigerian Academy of Science emphasized ethical AI and data-driven planning. Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology raised concerns on employment, local data and environmental impacts. National Academy of Sciences of Belarus highlighted telemedicine and data security National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Kazakhstan stressed technology access, SDG alignment and support for young scientists. Summarizing the deliberations, Prof. U. B. Desai , Vice President (Fellowship Affairs), INSA highlighted the need for enhanced cooperation, capacity building and knowledge exchange among member countries. The day also featured a Plenary Lecture by Prof. Anurag Agrawal , Vice President (Science Policy), INSA on the topic “Why AI in healthcare? (And When Not to Use It).” The formal proceedings of Day 01 concluded with discussions, followed by a cultural programme and networking dinner. The second day of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 concluded initiated with a plenary lecture by Prof. Indranil Manna , Vice President (Science & Society), INSA. He highlighted the role of AI in materials discovery, including data collection, pattern extraction, physics-based modelling and identification of promising material candidates. The keynote lecture by Dr. Ashish Lele , Director, CSIR-NCL, focused on “Harnessing AI and Green Hydrogen: Driving Efficiency and Decarbonization.” He outlined India’s energy transition pathway, the importance of the National Green Hydrogen Mission and the need for greener logistics and decarbonized data centres. A key highlight of the concluding day was the Open Discussion on the Joint Statement , chaired by Prof. Shekhar C. Mande , President, INSA, where representatives from BRICS member and partner science academies engaged in extensive deliberations to finalize a consensus communiqué. The Joint Statement , reflecting the shared vision and recommendations of the participating academies, is expected to be endorsed within a week and will be presented at the forthcoming BRICS Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Ministerial Meeting in August 2026 . In his concluding remarks, Shri Shambhulingappa Hakki , Joint Secretary (MER & G20) and BRICS Sous Sherpa emphasized that science is an indispensable pillar of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and evidence-based public policy. Congratulating the participating academies for arriving at a consensus communiqué, he remarked that the deliberations were both timely and aligned with India's vision of human-centric development. The proceedings concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr. Brajesh Pandey , Executive Director, INSA who expressed gratitude to all participating academies, delegates, speakers, IIT Hyderabad, MEA and INSA team for concluding the forum successfully. ***** NKR/FT (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289133) आगंतुक पटल  : 51 Ministry of Science & Technology Two Days of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 successfully concluded at IIT Hyderabad with focus on AI for Sustainability and Global South Cooperation प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Mine closure is a landmark initiative in India's transition towards circular economy: Dr Jitendra Singh
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology Mine closure is a landmark initiative in India's transition towards circular economy: Dr Jitendra Singh India's Mine Closure Journey Demonstrates Science Can Transform Environmental Challenges into Development Opportunities: Dr Jitendra Singh India's Scientific Mine Closure Model Can Inspire Sustainable Development Across Sectors: Dr Jitendra Singh Scientific Mine Closure Strengthens India's Journey Towards Net Zero and Sustainable Development: Dr Jitendra Singh प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi Describing the Mine closure as is a landmark initiative in India's transition towards circular economy, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology, Earth Sciences and Minister of State for the Prime Minister's Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today said that India is redefining the very idea of mine closure by transforming exhausted mines into new centres of wealth creation, environmental restoration and sustainable livelihoods. Referring to scientific mine closure as an embodiment of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of innovation-led governance, Dr. Jitendra Singh said a closed mine should no longer be viewed as the end of economic activity but as the beginning of a new development journey that serves both people and the planet. Dr. Jitendra Singh was addressing the release of "AAROH- Annual Report on Mine Closure", organised by the Ministry of Coal in New Delhi. The event was graced by Union Minister for Coal and Mines Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Minister of State for Coal and Mines Shri Satish Chandra Dubey, Secretary, Ministry of Coal Vikram Dev Dutt, senior officials of the Ministry, representatives of coal companies, industry leaders and international partners. The programme also witnessed the virtual inauguration of Coal NEER Plants, signing of the Implementation Agreement between the Ministry of Coal and GIZ for technical cooperation on closed coal mines, and Tripartite MoUs for establishing vocational training centres to create sustainable livelihood opportunities in coal-bearing regions. Calling the initiative a landmark in India's transition towards a circular economy, Dr. Jitendra Singh said scientific mine closure simultaneously advances several national priorities, including waste-to-wealth, resource efficiency, environmental conservation, sustainable land use and community development. "You have closed a coal mine and opened another mine of wealth," he remarked, describing the initiative as a powerful example of how science and technology can unlock fresh economic opportunities from assets that had long been considered exhausted. The Minister said such transformative thinking has become possible because the present Government encourages innovation instead of remaining confined to conventional approaches. He said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has consistently inspired institutions to challenge established practices and adopt bold, future-oriented solutions capable of delivering long-term national gains. Scientific mine closure, he said, represents one such policy innovation where environmental responsibility has been converted into an instrument of economic growth and social empowerment. Dr. Jitendra Singh said the initiative complements India's commitment to achieve Net Zero by 2070 by ensuring that environmental restoration progresses alongside economic development. He noted that as India expands renewable energy, nuclear energy and other emerging technologies, responsible utilisation and regeneration of natural resources will become equally important pillars of sustainable development. Progress, he said, must be measured not only by the efficiency with which resources are utilised but also by the responsibility with which they are restored for future generations. Appreciating the transformation documented through the 42 scientifically closed mines featured in AAROH, Dr. Jitendra Singh said these examples establish a practical roadmap for the future of post-mining land use in India. He said reclaimed mining areas can evolve into centres of economic activity by supporting agriculture, renewable energy, tourism, skill development and other community-centric initiatives. He also suggested expanding participation of self-help groups, particularly women's groups, so that scientific mine closure generates sustainable livelihood opportunities while strengthening local economies. Welcoming the Implementation Agreement between the Ministry of Coal and Germany's GIZ, Dr. Jitendra Singh said sustainable development increasingly depends upon collaborative partnerships that combine global expertise with local innovation. He described the agreement as a model capable of bringing together governments, scientific institutions and industry to accelerate scientific mine closure and land repurposing. Such collaborative frameworks, he said, have the potential to become replicable models across multiple sectors of the economy. The Minister stressed that successful public initiatives should be communicated in ways that inspire wider public participation. Referring to the visual documentation presented during the programme, he suggested preparing short digital films on each scientifically reclaimed mine so that citizens, administrators and stakeholders across the country can witness these transformations firsthand. Such storytelling, he said, would enable India's mine closure experience to become a national learning resource while encouraging similar innovations in other sectors. Drawing upon successful initiatives from other sectors, Dr. Jitendra Singh referred to the productive use of steel slag in road construction and the conversion of used cooking oil into biofuel, both of which initially appeared unconventional but eventually evolved into valuable economic resources. These experiences, he said, demonstrate that science-driven innovation has the power to convert waste into wealth while simultaneously generating public awareness, environmental benefits and new economic opportunities. He said the same philosophy lies at the heart of scientific mine closure, where yesterday's exhausted assets become tomorrow's engines of sustainable growth. The Ministry of Coal has been implementing a comprehensive framework for scientific mine closure that integrates ecological restoration, community development and sustainable post-mining land use. The AAROH- Annual Report on Mine Closure captures India's journey in scientifically closing 42 mines through detailed case studies, before-and-after documentation and digital resources, while showcasing best practices for future mine closure initiatives. Complementing these efforts are the revised Mine Closure Guidelines, the RECLAIM, LIVES and SUVIKALP frameworks, Coal NEER plants for productive utilisation of mine water, and partnerships aimed at strengthening international cooperation and community-centric development. Together, these initiatives reflect the Government's commitment to ensuring that every phase of mining contributes to sustainable and inclusive national development. ***** NKR/AK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289072) आगंतुक पटल  : 104 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Science & Technology Mine closure is a landmark initiative in India's transition towards circular economy: Dr Jitendra Singh India's Mine Closure Journey Demonstrates Science Can Transform Environmental Challenges into Development Opportunities: Dr Jitendra Singh India's Scientific Mine Closure Model Can Inspire Sustainable Development Across Sectors: Dr Jitendra Singh Scientific Mine Closure Strengthens India's Journey Towards Net Zero and Sustainable Development: Dr Jitendra Singh प्रविष्टि तिथि:

These experiences, he said, demonstrate that science-driven innovation has the power to convert waste into wealth while simultaneously generating public awareness, environmental benefits and new economic opportunities. He said the same philosophy lies at the heart of scientific mine closure, where yesterday's exhausted assets become tomorrow's engines of sustainable growth. The Ministry of Coal has been implementing a comprehensive framework for scientific mine closure that integrates ecological restoration, community development and sustainable post-mining land use. The AAROH- Annual Report on Mine Closure captures India's journey in scientifically closing 42 mines through detailed case studies, before-and-after documentation and digital resources, while showcasing best practices for future mine closure initiatives. Complementing these efforts are the revised Mine Closure Guidelines, the RECLAIM, LIVES and SUVIKALP frameworks, Coal NEER plants for productive utilisation of mine water, and partnerships aimed at strengthening international cooperation and community-centric development. Together, these initiatives reflect the Government's commitment to ensuring that every phase of mining contributes to sustainable and inclusive national development. ***** NKR/AK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289072)

title: Slew of technologies developed to enable electrically rechargeable Zinc-air batteries
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology Slew of technologies developed to enable electrically rechargeable Zinc-air batteries प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 2:50PM by PIB Delhi New nanofluid electrolyte developed by scientists which can enhance efficiency of the cathode of electrically rechargeable Zinc-air batteries offers potential for better, safer, cheaper, next generation green batteries. The electrolyte which is stable over three months, is directly applicable to the zinc-air battery industry and relevant to grid-scale storage and can support electric mobility in India. Conventionally, costly corrosion inhibitors are added to suppress zinc corrosion, but these often-hinder oxygen reaction kinetics. This challenge was solved by scientists from SASTRA Deemed University, Thanjavur, dispersed small amounts of inexpensive silica and zinc oxide nanoparticles into the standard electrolyte, creating "nanofluid electrolyte". This work supported by Department of Science and Technology (DST) under the Nano and Advanced Materials Division suppressed the hydrogen reaction while simultaneously inhibiting corrosion and enhancing oxygen reaction performance at the cathode, solving both electrode problems with one low-cost intervention. The technology protected by a granted Indian patent (IN570691), is ready for usage. As the world race toward cleaner energy storage, aqueous batteries are gaining attention as a safe, low-cost, environmentally friendly alternative to lithium-ion systems. Among them, the electrically rechargeable zinc-air battery (ZAB) stands out for its high theoretical energy density, low-cost, and water-based chemistry. The team led by Dr. S. Devaraj at SASTRA Deemed University, initiated efforts to resolve the two stubborn problems have held this green technology back -- unwanted hydrogen gas evolution at the zinc anode wastes charge and corrodes the metal, while oxygen reactions at the air-cathode remain sluggish without expensive platinum or ruthenium catalysts. Fig: Workflow of various strategies adopted to improve the kinetics of oxygen reactions at cathode and reduce hydrogen evolution reaction and zinc corrosion at the anode. Apart from engineering the nanofluid electrolyte to suppress parasitic hydrogen evolution and zinc corrosion simultaneously they developed earth-abundant bifunctional catalysts to drive both oxygen reduction (ORR) and oxygen evolution (OER) efficiently and explored waste-derived materials as viable electrode candidates. Their research identified α-MnO 2 as the top catalyst performer, owing to its open tunnel-like architecture. Strategic copper doping pushed performance beyond commercial benchmarks, outperforming both Pt- and Ru-based standards at a remarkably low dopant loading of just 2 wt%. They recovered spent activated carbon from exhausted household water filters and hydrothermally converted it into MnO 2 /C nanocomposites developing both efficient bifunctional electrocatalysts and high-performing supercapacitor electrodes. This process has been patented (Application No. 202441032753). Separately, post-pandemic surgical face masks were chemically upcycled into activated carbon with a record-high surface area, rivalling platinum in oxygen reduction activity. The approaches developed have prospects beyond this technology. The waste-derived carbon can be tuned for multiple applications beyond zinc-air batteries, and the upcycling approach is adaptable to virtually any waste carbon source. Similarly, the nanofluid electrolyte concept can potentially extend to other aqueous battery systems, offering a generalisable strategy for safer, cheaper, next-generation green batteries. For more details contact Dr. S. ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
title: DEVELOPMENT OF INLAND WATERWAYS AND RELATED PROJECTS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways DEVELOPMENT OF INLAND WATERWAYS AND RELATED PROJECTS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has embarked upon a transformational drive to promote Inland Water Transport (IWT) as a key pillar of India's multimodal transport system under Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. The primary objective encompasses creating world-class waterway infrastructure through fairway development, multimodal terminals, community jetties, river cruise terminals, regional centres of excellence, digital navigation tools, and green vessel technologies, coupled with seamless integration under the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan. The development and regulation of National Waterways (NWs) are spearheaded by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. To improve the Ease of Doing Business and simplify approvals, IWAI has introduced an array of digital reforms: PANI: Portal for Asset and Navigation Information to facilitate seamless navigation planning. Jalyan & Navic Portal: A centralized database and digital portal developed on the lines of 'Vahan' and 'Sarathi' for nationwide online registration of vessels and crew, enabling accurate tracking and strategic planning. CAR-D: Cargo Data Portal for real-time tracking and logistics data integration. Jal Samriddhi Portal: Dedicated portal supporting commercial and operational activities across National Waterways. Digital Charts and Hydrographic Surveys: Modern hydrographic charts provided digitally to Mariners for enhanced safety. These infrastructure, digital, and policy reforms have resulted in the operationalization of 32 National Waterways across the country, laying the foundation for a technology-driven, sustainable, and globally competitive IWT ecosystem that reduces logistics costs, promotes green mobility, and accelerates inclusive economic growth. LOGISTICS EFFICIENCY & ENVIRONMENTAL COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS Inland Water Transport serves as an economic and environmentally friendly alternate mode of transport to Rail and Road, significantly reducing congestion on existing transport networks. Economic Freight Cost Comparison (2014 Price Baseline) Inland Water Transport (IWT): Rs. 1.06 per Ton-Kilometer (TKm) Railways: Rs. 1.36 per Ton-Kilometer (TKm) Highways (Road): Rs. 2.50 per Ton-Kilometer (TKm) (Source: Ministry of Railways, TTSS, and IWAI) Environmental Impact & Emission Analysis Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions: IWT emits 0.0006 Rs/TKm, on par with Railways (0.0006 Rs/TKm) and significantly lower than Roadways (0.0031 Rs/TKm). Air Pollution Costs: IWT accounts for 0.03 Rs/TKm, compared to 0.0366 Rs/TKm for Railways and 0.202 Rs/TKm for Roadways. Noise, Soil & Water Pollution: IWT has negligible impact on noise, soil, and water pollution, whereas Road transport incurs 0.0032 Rs/TKm (noise) and 0.005 Rs/TKm (soil/water). (Source: 12th Five Year Plan, Planning Commission TTS Study, PIANC) POLICY MEASURES & SECTORAL REFORMS Jalvahak Scheme: A scheme providing 35% financial incentive to cargo owners and scheduled operators for cargo movement on NW-1, NW-2, and NW-16 via the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol (IBP) route by Inland & Coastal Shipping Limited (ICSL). Approved at a budget of Rs. 95.42 Crore for 3 years. Tonnage Tax Extension: Announced in the Union Budget on 01.02.2025, extending the special taxation system under the Indian Vessels Act, 2021 to inland vessels operating on NWs, rivers, and canals. Tax is calculated based on vessel size (tonnage) rather than net profit, ensuring stable, predictable, and lower tax burden. National Waterways Regulations 2025: Notified to provide a transparent regulatory framework that encourages private sector capital investment in building and operating inland waterways terminals and jetties. Cargo Aggregation & MMLPs: To resolve multimodality challenges arising from lack of industrial concentration along river banks, Multi-Modal Logistics Parks (MMLP) at Varanasi and Integrated Cluster-cum-Logistics Park at Sahibganj are being developed through NHLML (MoRTH). Rail connectivity to 3 MMTs is assigned to M/s Indian Port and Rail Company Ltd. PSU Cargo Shift Mandate: Over 140 Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) across key ministries (Petroleum & Natural Gas, Co-operation, Fertilizer, Food & Public Distribution, Heavy Industries, Steel, and Coal) have been engaged to mandate cargo allocation and modal shift to waterways. The Coastal Shipping Act, 2025: Enacted to modernize regulation at par with international standards, expand vessel chartering entities, reduce compliance burdens, and foster ease of doing business. Effective from 15.03.2026. Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme: Announced in Union Budget 2026–27 to increase the share of Inland Waterways and Coastal Shipping from 6% to 12% by 2047. IBP Route Operationalization: Indo-Bangladesh Protocol route No. 5 & 6 between Maia and Sultanganj has been operationalized with successful trial movements. REGIONAL WATERWAYS DEVELOPMENT & NATIONWIDE STATUS Northeast Region (NER) Waterways (NW-2 & NW-16) In addition to completed works (MMLP Jogighopa terminal, Bogibeel cargo-cum-tourist terminal, Dhubri & Bogibeel customs/immigration buildings, and NH-27 approach road), key ongoing projects include: Fairway development via Dredging Corporation of India (DCI) on NW-2 (Rs. 143 Crore). Ship Repair Facility at Pandu (revised cost Rs. 283 Crore). Tourist Jetty at Bishwanath Ghat & Cargo-cum-Cruise Terminal at Neamati Ghat (Rs. 158 Crore). Regional Centre of Excellence at Dibrugarh (Rs. 188 Crore). Steel Gangway with Yoke System at Pandu (Rs. 2.88 Crore). Regional Office, MSDC, Guest House & ITAT building at Fancy Bazar (Rs. 50.00 Crore). Link Road connecting Pandu Terminal with Ship Repair Facility (Rs. 55 Crore). 2 Steel Pontoons (Rs. 3.40 Crore) and 2 SDB Vessels (Rs. 2.88 Crore) for NW-2. Mathematical Modelling of Bogibeel Approach Channel (Rs. 0.60 Crore) and DPR for Community Jetties (Rs. 5.56 Crore). Southern Region Waterways (Kerala, Andhra Pradesh & Telangana) Kerala (NW-3, NW-8, NW-9): Continued fairway development on NW-3, NW-8 & NW-9. Reconstruction of navigation lock at Thrikunnapuzha and single-lane bridge at Kovilthottam entrusted to Kerala Govt on deposit basis. 24-hour navigational aids installed (15 in NW-8, 25 in NW-9) along with 4 HDPE jetties in NW-3. Andhra Pradesh & Telangana (NW-4): Land acquisition completed at Muktyala and Harichandrapuram; under progress at Ibrahimpatnam. Ro-Ro terminals developed at Muktyala and Harischandrapuram. 4 floating pontoon jetties handed over to APTDC; 3 steel floating pontoon jetties under fabrication for Krishna River in Telangana. Eastern, Western & Northern Region Waterways Odisha (NW-5, NW-14, NW-64): Regular thalweg surveys, 10 navigational buoys installed in Mahanadi River (NW-64), Talcher-Dhamra-Paradip stretch (NW-5) developed for coal evacuation, and 3 concrete jetties in NW-14 & NW-64. Karnataka (NW-51, NW-90): Development of Kabini River (NW-51) and Sharavati River (NW-90) for cruise tourism with 3 concrete jetties. Goa (NW-27, NW-68, NW-111): Mandovi, Zuari, and Cumberjua rivers developed for cruise tourism; 10 concrete jetties (including 4 floating concrete jetties on NW-68) provided. Gujarat (NW-73, NW-100): Development in Narmada River (NW-73) and Tapi River (NW-100) with 2 floating concrete jetties installed in Narmada and 2 in Tapi. West Bengal (NW-44, NW-97): Swaroopnagar single lane bridge across Ichamati River (NW-44) completed in March 2026 and inaugurated by Hon'ble PM. Sundarban Waterways (NW-97) 201 km international route maintained under PIWTT. UT of Jammu & Kashmir: Onshore facilities, floating concrete jetties, and nav aids initiated for Jhelum (NW-49), Chenab (NW-26), and Ravi (NW-84). Himachal Pradesh & Punjab: Feasibility studies underway for Beas River (NW-17) and Sutlej River (NW-98). List of Sagarmala- funded Projects in Andhra Pradesh IWAI initiated fairway development in the Vijayawada–Muktyala stretch (82 km) of NW-4 in 2014. The IWT terminal at Muktyala (NTR District) is completed, while Harischandrapuram (Guntur District) is underway. Updation of DPR for NW-4 (Kakinada–Puducherry Canal integrated with Krishna & Godavari) is ongoing. The Commamuru Canal (113 km from Vijayawada to Pedaganjam Lock) passes through Bapatla District, connecting NW-4 with the North Buckingham Canal towards Chennai. HYDROGRAPHIC NAVIGATION & RIS INFRASTRUCTURE Hydrographic Survey Expansion: Regular weekly, fortnightly, or monthly thalweg surveys are carried out across 22 National Waterways (NW-1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 14, 16, 23, 31, 40, 44, 47, 57, 64, 73, 86, 94, 97, 100, 110) and the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol route to assess navigational channels and fairway conditions. River Information System (RIS): Implemented on NW-1 (Ganga) across Haldia–Farakka (Phase-I), Farakka–Patna (Phase-II), and Patna–Varanasi (Phase-III). Features 4 Control Stations, 13 Base Stations, AIS, VHF communication, meteorological sensors, and RIS consoles on 30 departmental vessels for real-time traffic monitoring. Electronic Navigational Charts (ENCs): Prepared and uploaded on PANI and IWAI Vessel Tracker for 17 operational/tidal waterways (NW-1, 3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 14, 23, 27, 53, 64, 68, 73, 83, 86, 91, 110, 111). Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways SAGARMALA PROGRAMME AND PORT MODERNISATION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi Sagarmala scheme is a central sector scheme of Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) with the target to promote port-led development in the country. Under this scheme, MoPSW provides financial assistance for the projects under 5 pillars namely, port modernization, port connectivity, port-led industrialization, coastal community development, and coastal shipping & inland water transport. The pillar wise progress of the projects funded under Sagarmala scheme is available at Annexure-I. Annexure I Details of Completed and under Implementation projects pillar wise under Sagarmala Scheme : Pillars Completed projects Under implementation projects Number Cost (₹ Cr) Number Cost (₹ Cr) Coastal Shipping and IWT 25 1178.5 17 1167.7 Coastal Community Development 19 1912.6 28 3008.4 Port Modernization 18 870.2 6 160.8 Port Connectivity 17 1413.2 3 201.3 Grand Total 79 5374.5 54 4538.2 Government has taken several measures to enhance port capacity, improve operational efficiency, and reduce vessel turnaround time at major ports. Infrastructure development and capacity augmentation is a continuous process and includes construction of new berths and terminals, mechanization, modernization and optimization of existing berths and terminals, capital dredging to deepen drafts for accommodating larger vessels, development of road and rail connectivity, and creation of supporting infrastructure such as parking plazas. Further, port processes have been streamlined with the implementation of One Nation One Port Process (ONOP) to improve operational efficiency and reduce vessel turnaround time. As a result of these initiatives, the cargo handling capacity of the Major and Other than Major Ports (OTMP) has increased to 2,818 Million Tonnes Per Annum (MTPA) as on March 2026 from ~1,400 MTPA in 2013-14. One of the objectives of Sagarmala programme is better port connectivity, efficient cargo movement between ports and their respective hinterland to minimize overall logistics cost. Sagarmala programme has a dedicated pillar of port connectivity which focuses on the last mile and immediate hinterland connectivity of the ports via road, rail and inland waterways. Further, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) has undertaken a comprehensive assessment of port connectivity and prepared a Comprehensive Port Connectivity Plan (CPCP) in 2022 by reviewing connectivity of the operational ports and identified the ports which needed improvement of road and/ or rail connectivity with nearby economic hubs. Subsequently, MoPSW in consultation with Ministry of Road, Transport and Highways and Ministry of Railways has identified a total of 294 rail and road connectivity projects, out of which, 84 projects (63 Rail and 21 Road) have been completed, 66 projects (27 Rail and 39 Road) are under implementation, and a total of 144 projects (42 Rail and 102 Road) are under planning stage. The connectivity projects within the port limits are taken up by the Port Authorities and beyond the port limits are taken up by Ministries like MoR, MoRTH or State Governments. As regard to inland waterway connectivity projects, details of projects completed by Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI) on National Waterways (NW) are as under: 3 Multi Modal Terminals (MMTs) and 01 intermodal terminal on NW 1 1 MMT and 3 IWT terminals on NW 2 9 IWT terminals on NW 3; 02 Roll-on/Roll-off (Ro-Ro) terminals in Ernakulam 01 Ro-Ro terminal on NW 4 The MoPSW has sanctioned financial assistance of ₹ 272 crore to 9 projects worth ₹ 1,286 crore under Sagarmala scheme in the state of Andhra Pradesh and the details of these projects are available at Annexure-II. ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
title: REVAMPING OF SHIPBUILDING INDUSTRY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways REVAMPING OF SHIPBUILDING INDUSTRY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi The Government has reviewed India's Shipbuilding sector following the  announcement of measures under the Union Budget 2025–26 and adopted a 4-pillar  strategy to revitalize the shipbuilding sector. The Government has accordingly approved a  comprehensive package of ₹ 69,725 crore to strengthen domestic shipbuilding  capacity, maritime financing and skilling. The key components of the shipbuilding  package include: Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS), an extension of  Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP), with outlay of ₹ 24,736 crore to  address cost disadvantages of Indian shipyards vis-a-vis global shipyards; Maritime Development Fund (MDF) corpus of ₹ 25,000 crore for providing long  term financing support to shipbuilding and maritime sector comprising a Maritime  Investment Fund (MIF) of ₹ 20,000 crore and Interest Incentivisation Fund (IIF) of ₹  5,000 crore; Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SbDS) with ₹19,989 crore outlay to expand  Indian shipbuilding output capacity to 4.5 million Gross Tonnage annually by setting up greenfield shipbuilding clusters and capacity expansion of the existing  shipyards. These targets have been set to position India as a competitive global  shipbuilding force in line with the vision contained in Maritime India Vision 2030 and  Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 documents. Policy reforms have been undertaken to revamp the shipbuilding industry including  implementation of classification of large vessels as infrastructure and demand  aggregation. The government on 19th September 2025, notified infrastructure status to  Indian-flagged commercial vessels with a Gross Tonnage (GT) of 10,000 or above. For  vessels constructed in India infrastructure status was accorded to vessels of size 1,500  GT or above. As part of demand aggregation, a fleet acquisition plan of 400+ vessels  has been prepared which provides long term order visibility to the Indian shipyards. The scheme guidelines to operationalize SBFAS have been issued on  26.12.2025 and in-principle approvals for shipbuilding financial support are given in  accordance with scheme guidelines. The guidelines for MDF have also been issued  on 20.02.2026. Further, SBI Ventures Limited has been appointed as the Fund  Manager for MIF on 26.05.2026. As on-date, under SbDS, Government has accorded in-principle approval for  the development of three greenfield shipbuilding clusters at Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat  and Tamil Nadu. SbDS provides financial assistance for development of common  maritime and land based infrastructure for the greenfield clusters. Further, under SbDS,  the India Ship Technology Centre (ISTC) has been established as a Section 8 company  to promote the overall development of the Indian shipbuilding sector by enhancing  capabilities in ship design, research and development (R&D), skill development,  software, and other related areas. As regards skilling development, the details of  various steps taken are as under: 11 shipyards have signed MoUs with 34 ITIs across 8 coastal States towards  implementation of on the job training (OJTs). As part of this, a 150-hour OJT model has  been introduced. 727 trainees have already been trained till date in these yards. Training of Trainers (ToT) program has been implemented at 2 Industrial  Training Institutes (ITIs) in West Bengal by Centre of Excellence in Maritime and  Shipbuilding (CEMS). A preliminary Skill Gap Study has been completed across 9 shipyards. A total of 92,697 candidates have been trained/skilled/upskilled during the last  3 years. A Plan of Implementation (PoI) has been signed between MoPSW and Korea  International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) for a skill development project in the  shipbuilding sector. As per the latest UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) report, India’s  shipbuilding output increased by 41% from 40,923 GT in 2024 to 57,637 GT in 2025 .  The comprehensive shipbuilding package of Government of India has instilled  confidence in Indian shipyards, resulting in the placement of several large commercial  and export shipbuilding orders to existing shipyards. In the last two years in-principle  approvals have been given for financial assistance under SBFAP and SPFAS to the Indian  shipyards for a total contract value of ₹15,234 crore. Under the SbDS scheme, so far,  in-principle approval has been given to proposals of four shipyards for brownfield  capacity augmentation of their facilities for ship-building and ship-repair at a total estimated cost of over ₹2,500 crore. Given the high employment multiplier of 6.4 in the shipbuilding industry, the above developments have catalysed generation of large numbers of direct as well as indirect employment. This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha. *** MI/Indu (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288924) आगंतुक पटल  : 101 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways REVAMPING OF SHIPBUILDING INDUSTRY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                        24 JUL 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi The Government has reviewed India's Shipbuilding sector following the  announcement of measures under the Union Budget 2025–26 and adopted a 4-pillar  strategy to revitalize the shipbuilding sector. The Government has accordingly approved a  comprehensive package of ₹ 69,725 crore to strengthen domestic shipbuilding  capacity, maritime financing and skilling. The key components of the shipbuilding  package include: Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Scheme (SBFAS), an extension of  Shipbuilding Financial Assistance Policy (SBFAP), with outlay of ₹ 24,736 crore to  address cost disadvantages of Indian shipyards vis-a-vis global shipyards; Maritime Development Fund (MDF) corpus of ₹ 25,000 crore for providing long  term financing support to shipbuilding and maritime sector comprising a Maritime  Investment Fund (MIF) of ₹ 20,000 crore and Interest Incentivisation Fund (IIF) of ₹  5,000 crore; Shipbuilding Development Scheme (SbDS) with ₹19,989 crore outlay to expand  Indian shipbuilding output capacity to 4.5 million Gross Tonnage annually by setting up greenfield shipbuilding clusters and capacity expansion of the existing  shipyards. These targets have been set to position India as a competitive global  shipbuilding force in line with the vision contained in Maritime India Vision 2030 and  Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 documents. Policy reforms have been undertaken to revamp the shipbuilding industry including  implementation of classification of large vessels as infrastructure and demand  aggregation. The government on 19th September 2025, notified infrastructure status to  Indian-flagged commercial vessels with a Gross Tonnage (GT) of 10,000 or above. For  vessels constructed in India infrastructure status was accorded to vessels of size 1,500  GT or above. As part of demand aggregation, a fleet acquisition plan of 400+ vessels  has been prepared which provides long term order visibility to the Indian shipyards. The scheme guidelines to operationalize SBFAS have been issued on  26.12.2025 and in-principle approvals for shipbuilding financial support are given in  accordance with scheme guidelines. The guidelines for MDF have also been issued  on 20.02.2026. Further, SBI Ventures Limited has been appointed as the Fund  Manager for MIF on 26.05.2026. As on-date, under SbDS, Government has accorded in-principle approval for  the development of three greenfield shipbuilding clusters at Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat  and Tamil Nadu. SbDS provides financial assistance for development of common  maritime and land based infrastructure for the greenfield clusters. Further, under SbDS,  the India Ship Technology Centre (ISTC) has been established as a Section 8 company  to promote the overall development of the Indian shipbuilding sector by enhancing  capabilities in ship design, research and development (R&D), skill development,  software, and other related areas. As regards skilling development, the details of  various steps taken are as under: 11 shipyards have signed MoUs with 34 ITIs across 8 coastal States towards  implementation of on the job training (OJTs). As part of this, a 150-hour OJT model has  been introduced. 727 trainees have already been trained till date in these yards. Training of Trainers (ToT) program has been implemented at 2 Industrial  Training Institutes (ITIs) in West Bengal by Centre of Excellence in Maritime and  Shipbuilding (CEMS). A preliminary Skill Gap Study has been completed across 9 shipyards. A total of 92,697 candidates have been trained/skilled/upskilled during the last  3 years. A Plan of Implementation (PoI) has been signed between MoPSW and Korea  International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) for a skill development project in the  shipbuilding sector. As per the latest UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) report, India’s  shipbuilding output increased by 41% from 40,923 GT in 2024 to 57,637 GT in 2025 .  The comprehensive shipbuilding package of Government of India has instilled  confidence in Indian shipyards, resulting in the placement of several large commercial  and export shipbuilding orders to existing shipyards. In the last two years in-principle  approvals have been given for financial assistance under SBFAP and SPFAS to the Indian  shipyards for a total contract value of ₹15,234 crore. Under the SbDS scheme, so far,  in-principle approval has been given to proposals of four shipyards for brownfield  capacity augmentation of their facilities for ship-building and ship-repair at a total estimated cost of over ₹2,500 crore. Given the high employment multiplier of 6.4 in the shipbuilding industry, the above developments have catalysed generation of large numbers of direct as well as indirect employment. This information was given by the Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal, in a written reply to the Lok Sabha. *** MI/Indu (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288924)

title: EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN MARITIME SECTOR
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN MARITIME SECTOR प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi To strengthen employment opportunities in the maritime sector, the Government has undertaken a multi-pronged strategy for capacity building. Since completion of onboard sea-time training is an essential requirement for certification and career progression, initiatives have been taken to augment training capacity, strengthen industry participation and create additional onboard training opportunities, thereby enhancing the employability of Indian maritime trainees and supporting the long-term growth of the maritime workforce. As part of these initiatives, 96 training berths have been created on the passenger vessel MV Swaraj Dweep of the Andaman & Nicobar Administration in collaboration with the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), benefiting General Purpose (GP) Rating and Certificate Course in Maritime Catering (CCMC) candidates. To promote cargo transportation and economic activities through the development of inland waterways, Government declared 111 (5 pre-existing and 106 new) National Waterways (NWs) in the country vide National Waterways Act, 2016. Action plans for development for NWs have been drawn under Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 by the Government. Initiatives as Infrastructure and Policy measures taken to promote cargo transportation through the inland water transportation are detailed at Annexure-1 . Due to these measures, the cargo movement on National Waterways increased from 18 million tons in 2013-14 to 218 million tons in 2025-26. Details of cargo transportation through inland waterways year-wise, from 2014 to 2026 and active seafarers are placed at Annexure-2 . Annexure-1 Infrastructure and Policy measures taken by the Government for promotion and modernize Inland Water Transport on NWs: Infrastructure measures: Fairway maintenance works (river training, maintenance dredging, channel marking and regular hydrographic surveys) are taken up in various National Waterways (NWs) for providing a navigation channel of 35/45 m width and 2.0 / 2.2 / 2.5 / 3.0 m least available depth (LAD) for operation of vessels. 66 community jetties, 20 floating terminals, 3 Multi-Modal Terminals (MMTs), 1 Inter-Modal Terminal (IMT) and 4 Ro-Pax terminals have been constructed on NW-1 (River Ganga) in addition to 5 pre-existing permanent terminals. 13 floating terminals provided on NW-2 (River Brahmaputra) along with MMTs at Pandu, Jogighopa and terminals at Bogibeel and Dhubri. Four dedicated Jetties for cruise vessels have been provided at Jogighopa, Pandu, Biswanath Ghat and Neamati. In addition to this, Jetties for cruise and passengers have been constructed at Sadiya, Lyka and Orium Ghat in Assam. 2 existing terminals at Badarpur & Karimganj on NW-16 (the Barak) have been upgraded/renovated and the terminal at Sonamura on river Gumati in Tripura under IBP route has been constructed. 9 Permanent Inland Water Transport terminals with godowns and 2 Ro-Ro/Ro-Pax terminals have been constructed on NW-3 (West Coast Canal in Kerala). 4 floating concrete jetties were provided to the Govt. of Goa and installed in Mandovi River (NW-68). 04 Tourist Jetties on NW-4 (River Krishna) in Andhra Pradesh have been commissioned and 8 Nos. floating jetties on NW-110 (River Yamuna) in Mathura-Vrindavan stretch in Uttar Pradesh, 2 Jetties on NW-73 (River Narmada) & 2 Jetties on NW-37 (River Gandak) in Bihar are established. A new Navigation Lock at Farakka and 2 Nos. Quick Pontoon Opening Mechanisms (QPOMs) have been constructed on NW-1 to facilitate smooth & faster movement of vessels. Policy Measures: A scheme for providing 35% incentive to promote the utilization of inland waterways transport sector by cargo owners and for scheduled service for cargo movement on NW-1 and NW-2 and NW-16 via Indo Bangladesh Protocol by Inland & Coastal Shipping Limited (ICSL) has been approved by the Government. This scheme is expected to divert 800 million tonne Km cargo on IWT mode, which is nearly 17% of the current cargo of 4700 million tonne Km on NWs. The scheme is implemented at a cost of INR 95.42 Crore for three years and can be scaled up or modified depending on the success of the scheme. An extension of the tonnage tax scheme to inland vessels registered under the Indian Vessels Act, 2021 is announced during the budget presented on 01.02.2025. Inland vessels operating on National Waterways, rivers, and canals, will be benefited. This move is expected to boost the industry's competitiveness and encourage more cargo owners to use inland waterways for transportation. A tonnage tax system is a special taxation policy for shipping companies where tax is not based on actual profits but on the size (tonnage) of the vessel. It provides stable, predictable, and lower taxation for vessel owners, reducing their financial burden. The National Waterways (Construction of Jetties / Terminals) Regulations 2025 has been notified, allowing private companies to invest and operate Inland Waterways infrastructure by providing a clear regulatory framework to attract private sector investment for facilitating the growth of inland waterways sector. Jalyan & Navic : To increase ease of doing business in the IWT sector, along the same lines as ‘vahan’ and ‘sarathi’, a central data base and portal has been developed for registration of vessels and crew all over the country. This will facilitate registration of vessels and crew digitally and would also provide accurate status on the number of vessels and crew in the country and thus help in planning. Cargo Aggregation : The cargo movement on the waterways suffer from problems of multimodality because of lack of industries along the waterways. Therefore, projects for development of cargo aggregation hub – MMLP at Varanasi and Integrated Cluster-cum-Logistics Park, Sahibganj have been taken up. NHLML, a PSU under the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has been engaged for development of these MMLPs. The work of Rail connectivity for three MMTs has been assigned to M/s Indian Port and Rail Company Ltd. (A PSU under MoPSW). IBP Route : Indo Bangladesh Protocol route no. 5 & 6 between Maia and Sultanganj has been operationalized recently with successful trial movements. Regular movement shall commence shortly, once the consent of Bangladesh Side is received. Shift of cargo by PSUs : For modal shift of cargo to waterways, more than 140 Public Sector Units have been approached to plan their movement using Inland Water Transport mode. They have been requested to outline their current status of cargo movement through the waterways and their plan for modal shift of cargo. The Ministry of PNG, Co-operation/ Fertiliser, Food & Public distribution, Heavy industries, Steel and Coal have been requested to advise the PSUs under their jurisdiction to utilise IWT mode as far as possible and earmark certain percentage of their cargo for IWT mode keeping in line the MIV targets. title: Five Senior Citizen Homes Inaugurated Across Five States; MoU Signed to Strengthen Elderly Welfare; Innovative Programmes Promote Inter-generational Bonding
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Five Senior Citizen Homes Inaugurated Across Five States; MoU Signed to Strengthen Elderly Welfare; Innovative Programmes Promote Inter-generational Bonding प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi The government continues to strengthen its commitment towards ensuring the dignity, security and well-being of senior citizens through comprehensive initiatives under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) . Commemorating the International Day of Older Persons (IDOP) 2025 , the Department organised a series of nationwide programmes to promote healthy ageing, social inclusion, legal awareness and inter-generational bonding among senior citizens. This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B.L. Verma in a written reply to Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal in the Lok Sabha. The nationwide celebrations highlighted the Government's sustained efforts to create an age-friendly society while encouraging active participation of senior citizens in community life. The initiatives also complemented the objectives of AVYAY by strengthening partnerships with institutions, civil society organisations and local communities. As part of the celebrations, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed with the Birla Open Minds Foundation to promote collaborative initiatives for the welfare and empowerment of senior citizens. The Department also virtually inaugurated five Senior Citizen Homes located in Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Assam, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand , further expanding institutional care and support infrastructure for elderly citizens across the country. To encourage stronger family values and inter-generational engagement, the Department launched "Naitik Patham" , an interactive educational game designed to promote meaningful interaction between younger and older generations. A QR Code-based initiative for Grandparents-Teachers Meetings was also introduced to foster greater involvement of senior citizens in children's educational development. The celebrations included inter-generational bonding programmes in Jabalpur, Badaun, Chhatarpur, Navgaon, Biaora and Mount Abu , bringing together youth and senior citizens through interactive activities. In collaboration with S-VYASA, Bengaluru , yoga sessions and health camps were organised to promote healthy and active ageing among elderly citizens. Recognising the importance of legal awareness, a special session on the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 was organised in collaboration with the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) . The programme focused on creating awareness regarding the legal rights, welfare provisions and social security measures available to senior citizens while encouraging families and communities to fulfil their responsibilities towards elderly members. A cultural programme titled "Aradhana" was also organised to celebrate the invaluable contribution of senior citizens to society and to encourage their active participation in cultural and community life. Through these initiatives, the Government reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that every senior citizen lives with dignity, respect, security and access to quality care. Under the umbrella of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) , the Ministry continues to work in convergence with State Governments, autonomous bodies and civil society organisations to build an inclusive and supportive ecosystem for senior citizens across the country. *** PR – 031 – TAR/KV/GA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289125) आगंतुक पटल  : 73 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Five Senior Citizen Homes Inaugurated Across Five States; MoU Signed to Strengthen Elderly Welfare; Innovative Programmes Promote Inter-generational Bonding प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Over 13,550 Scheduled Caste Students in Karnataka's Chikkaballapura District Benefit Under Central Scholarship Schemes: MoS for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale in Written Reply in Lok Sabha
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Over 13,550 Scheduled Caste Students in Karnataka's Chikkaballapura District Benefit Under Central Scholarship Schemes: MoS for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale in Written Reply in Lok Sabha 8,460 Students Receive Post-Matric Scholarship While 5,090 Students Benefit Under Pre-Matric Scholarship During Academic Year 2025–26 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 6:29PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is continuously strengthening the implementation of Centrally Sponsored Scholarship Schemes to ensure equitable access to quality education for Scheduled Caste (SC) students across the country. Through technology-enabled service delivery, Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) and sustained awareness initiatives, the Ministry is ensuring timely financial assistance, enhanced transparency and efficient delivery of scholarship benefits to eligible students. This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri Ramdas Athawale in a written reply to Dr. K Sudhakar in the Lok Sabha. The Minister informed the House that the Department is implementing three major scholarship schemes for Scheduled Caste students, namely the Post-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes (PMS-SC) , the Pre-Matric Scholarship for Scheduled Castes and Others , and the SHREYAS – Scholarships for Higher Education for Young Achievers Scheme for Scheduled Castes . These schemes aim to reduce financial barriers and promote access to quality education among Scheduled Caste students. During the Academic Year 2025–26 , 8,460 students from Chikkaballapura district of Karnataka benefited under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme , while 5,090 students received assistance under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme , taking the total number of beneficiaries to 13,550 . No beneficiary from the district availed assistance under the SHREYAS-SC Scheme during the same period. The Minister further informed that the Ministry introduced the Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mechanism under the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme in 2021–22 and under the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme in 2022–23 . The DBT system has significantly improved scholarship delivery by ensuring direct transfer of funds into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts of beneficiaries, eliminating duplication, reducing delays and enhancing transparency in fund disbursement. The technology-driven system has particularly benefited students residing in rural and semi-urban areas by ensuring timely receipt of financial assistance. To ensure that eligible students are fully aware of the available scholarship schemes, the Department has undertaken extensive awareness and outreach activities across the country. These include advertisements in national and regional newspapers, social media campaigns, continuous engagement with States and Union Territories, regular monitoring through National Chintan Shivirs, regional review meetings and national conferences with State Governments and other stakeholders to improve coverage and implementation of the schemes. The written reply further stated that while the Department has not independently assessed changes in dropout rates among Scheduled Caste students at the higher secondary and graduation levels, an evaluation conducted by NITI Aayog has observed that the scholarship schemes have played a significant role in promoting educational equity by reducing financial constraints and encouraging continuation of higher education among students belonging to disadvantaged communities. The evaluation also noted an improvement in scholarship disbursement following the introduction of the DBT system. Regarding revision of maintenance allowance under the scholarship schemes, the Minister informed the House that any revision is undertaken in consultation with all concerned stakeholders in accordance with the prescribed Government procedures. The Government remains committed to empowering Scheduled Caste students through inclusive and transparent scholarship programmes that promote educational opportunities, reduce financial barriers and strengthen social justice. Through sustained reforms, digital governance and continuous engagement with States and stakeholders, the Ministry continues to ensure that no eligible student is deprived of educational assistance due to financial constraints. title: Government Issues Model Guidelines for Development and Regulation of Retirement Homes for Senior Citizens: MoS for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma in Written Reply in Rajya Sabha
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Issues Model Guidelines for Development and Regulation of Retirement Homes for Senior Citizens: MoS for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma in Written Reply in Rajya Sabha Model Guidelines Aim to Promote Safe, Accessible and Well-Regulated Retirement Homes Across the Country प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 4:42PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has formulated and circulated Model Guidelines for the Development and Regulation of Retirement Homes to all States and Union Territories with the objective of promoting safe, accessible and dignified living conditions for senior citizens. The initiative seeks to provide a comprehensive framework for the establishment, operation and regulation of retirement homes while encouraging States and Union Territories to strengthen their regulatory mechanisms. This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma in a written reply to Shri Neerja Dangi in the Rajya Sabha. The Minister informed the House that 'Land' and 'Colonization' are State subjects under Entry 18 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution. However, in view of the increasing need for quality residential facilities for the elderly, the Central Government has prepared the Model Guidelines to serve as a reference framework for States and Union Territories in developing policies and regulations for retirement homes. The Minister further stated that the Model Guidelines prescribe essential standards to ensure that retirement homes are designed to meet the needs of senior citizens. These include the provision of wheelchair-accessible ramps and lifts, wide corridors with handrails, uninterrupted water supply, power backup facilities, ambulance services and in-apartment panic alarm systems to facilitate prompt emergency response. The guidelines are aimed at creating elderly-friendly infrastructure that promotes safety, accessibility and independent living for residents. The written reply also stated that retirement homes are covered under the provisions of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA) . Consequently, such projects are required to comply with the transparency, accountability and consumer protection measures applicable to other real estate developments, thereby strengthening confidence among senior citizens and their families. The Government remains committed to promoting the welfare and dignity of senior citizens by encouraging the development of safe, accessible and professionally managed retirement homes. Through the Model Guidelines, the Ministry seeks to support States and Union Territories in creating a robust regulatory ecosystem that ensures quality services, enhanced safety standards and a better quality of life for the elderly across the country.
