title: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) observed Swachhata Pakhwada from 1st to 15th July,2026 across the country
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) observed Swachhata Pakhwada  from 1st to 15th July,2026 across the country प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) observed Swachhata Pakhwada 2026 from 1st to 15th July 2026 with active participation of all Divisions, Attached /Subordinate/ Autonomous Organisations and Field level Offices of the Ministry  located across the country. The Swachhata Pakhwada commenced with the administration of the Swachhata Pledge and a wide cleanliness drive aimed at reinforcing the commitment towards cleanliness, environmental sustainability and efficient workplace management. A comprehensive day-wise action plan was prepared covering activities such as office cleanliness drives, record weeding and review of old files, disposal of obsolete and unserviceable items, digital housekeeping and promotion of e-office practices. Special emphasis was laid on improving office surroundings and enhancing workplace hygiene. During the fortnight, various Divisions and Offices of the Ministry as well as field offices of MoSPI located across the country organized a wide range of activities including plantation drives, Swachhata awareness campaigns, seminars, workshops, quiz competitions, essay and poster competitions, rallies, shramdaan programmes and community outreach initiatives aimed at promoting public awareness on cleanliness and environmental protection. The Ministry also undertook initiatives related to reduction of single-use plastic, waste segregation, recycling and sustainable waste management practices in line with the objectives of the Government of India's Swachh Bharat Mission. As part of the Pakhwada, best practices and innovative initiatives undertaken by various Divisions and Regional Offices were documented and disseminated across the Ministry to encourage wider adoption and institutionalization of successful cleanliness initiatives. The Swachhata Pakhwada concluded on 15 July 2026 with activities undertaken, sharing of achievements and recognition of significant contributions made by various offices and officials towards strengthening the culture of cleanliness within the Ministry. The Ministry reaffirms its commitment towards the vision of a cleaner, healthier and more sustainable India and calls upon all officials and stakeholders to actively participate in the Swachhata movement. "Swachhata is not merely an activity, but a collective responsibility and a way of life." Policy Initiatives/Industry Initiatives Hon’ble Union Minister of Steel Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy visited SAIL’s IISCO Steel Plant to review key expansion projects, production facilities, infrastructure, sustainability initiatives and employee welfare measures. During the visit, he inaugurated an 84,000 m³ RCC water reservoir, describing it as an important step towards building sustainable industrial infrastructure and reaffirming the Government’s commitment to capacity expansion and modernization of the steel sector. SAIL announced that Bokaro Steel Plant will receive around 8.3 MT of iron ore annually through India's longest steel-sector slurry pipeline. The 258-km Jamda–Bokaro pipeline will ensure uninterrupted raw material supply, reduce dependence on rail transport, and support the plant's expansion programme. MECON and RITES signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to jointly pursue consultancy and infrastructure projects in India and overseas. The partnership will leverage their expertise in transport, metals, mining and energy sectors to deliver integrated infrastructure solutions and expand their global footprint. India's crude steelmaking capacity reached approximately 222 MTPA as of June 2026, progressing towards the National Steel Policy target of 300 MTPA by 2030. Marking a key step in this direction, Bhilai Steel Plant signed an EPCM consultancy agreement with MECON to support the timely execution of its expansion from 7 MTPA to 10.2 MTPA through advanced engineering and construction management practices. 7. International Co-operation SAIL signed an MoU with Indonesia's PT Krakatau Steel to explore a joint venture for manufacturing stainless steel slabs in Indonesia. The proposed collaboration will combine Indonesia's nickel resources with SAIL's steelmaking expertise, strengthening the regional stainless steel value chain and enhancing India–Indonesia industrial cooperation. 8. Green Steel Initiatives SAIL received the Golden Peacock Environment Management Award 2026 from the Institute of Directors (IOD) in recognition of its excellence in environmental sustainability. The award acknowledges the company's initiatives in decarbonisation, pollution control, waste management, and adoption of sustainable steelmaking practices. Under the Ministry of Steel's Green Steel Initiative, 97 producers across 15 states had been issued Green Steel Certificates. title: 'Weaves of India' Festival Showcases India's Finest Handloom Heritage at Central Cottage Industries Emporium
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles 'Weaves of India' Festival Showcases India's Finest Handloom Heritage at Central Cottage Industries Emporium The festival is open to visitors  from 24 July to 7 August 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi The Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, is organizing the 'Weaves of India' Festival at the Central Cottage Industries Emporium (CCIE), Janpath, New Delhi. The festival will remain open to the public from 24 July to 7 August 2026 as part of the celebrations leading up to 12 th National Handloom Day on 7 th of August. The festival presents a curated celebration of India's rich and diverse handloom traditions, bringing together exemplary handwoven creations representing 116 heritage weaves from across the country. It offers visitors an opportunity to experience the extraordinary craftsmanship, artistic excellence and cultural legacy preserved by generations of Indian weavers. The exhibition features celebrated weaving traditions from Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Manipur, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Telangana, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir and Tripura , among others. Visitors can explore iconic handloom traditions including Banarasi, Jamdani, Kanchipuram Silk, SambalpuriIkat, Paithani, Kani Pashmina, BawanButi, Kotpad, Ilkal,Kasargod, Himroo and Risha , each representing the unique cultural identity and textile heritage of its region. Beyond showcasing exceptional textiles, the festival aims to strengthen public appreciation for authentic handwoven products while creating greater awareness about sustainable, ethical and artisan-led production systems. It also provides a valuable platform for interaction between master weavers, designers, collectors, buyers, researchers and the general public. The Government of India remains committed to preserving, promoting and revitalising the country's rich handloom heritage through sustained support for artisans, design innovation, market development and consumer awareness. The 'Weaves of India' Festival reflects this commitment by celebrating India's living textile traditions and encouraging citizens to support the country's handloom artisans. The festival is open to visitors at the Central Cottage Industries Emporium, Janpath, New Delhi , from 24 July to 7 August 2026 . Members of the public are invited to witness the timeless elegance and unparalleled artistry of India's handwoven heritage. ****** MAM/VN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2289127) आगंतुक पटल  : 65 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu Ministry of Textiles 'Weaves of India' Festival Showcases India's Finest Handloom Heritage at Central Cottage Industries Emporium The festival is open to visitors  from 24 July to 7 August 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: TRADE PREPAREDNESS AND EXPORT COMPETITIVENESS OF TEXTILE SECTOR
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles TRADE PREPAREDNESS AND EXPORT COMPETITIVENESS OF TEXTILE SECTOR प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 2:48PM by PIB Delhi India’s exports of textiles and apparel, including handicrafts, stood at ₹3,25,339 crore in 2025–26, registering a growth of 1.8 per cent over ₹3,19,573.2 crore in 2024–25 with export growth recorded in over 100 countries. The Government has implemented several schemes and undertaken various initiatives to strengthen the global competitiveness and export preparedness of the Textile and Apparel sector. These inter-alia includes the PM Mega Integrated Textile Regions and Apparel Parks Scheme (including at Amravati, Maharashtra), the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Textiles, the National Technical Textiles Mission, SAMARTH - Scheme for Capacity Building in the Textile Sector, and the launch of various components including Market Access Support and interest subvention under the Export Promotion Mission etc. In addition, several measures have recently been undertaken to support the Textile and Apparel exports and address emerging global challenges. These include the extension of Remission of Duties and Taxes on Exported Products Scheme up to 30 September 2026; the temporary exemption from customs duty on import of Cotton falling under Customs Tariff Heading 5201 from 1 June to 31 October 2026; the temporary exemption from customs duties on key inputs in the man-made fibre (MMF) value chain, including Purified Terephthalic Acid and Mono-Ethylene Glycol ; rationalisation of GST rates for correcting of the inverted duty structure in the MMF value chain; and the launch of the Resilience & Logistics Intervention for Export Facilitation (RELIEF) initiative to support exporters affected by disruptions arising from the evolving geopolitical situation in West Asia and its continuing impact on maritime logistics across the Gulf and adjoining regions. The Rebate of State and Central Taxes and Levies (RoSCTL) Scheme, operational since March 2019, provides for the rebate of embedded State and Central taxes and levies on the export of garments and made-ups, with a view to enhancing the competitiveness of these sectors. The Scheme has been extended for a further period of six months, up to 30 September 2026, to ensure policy predictability and stability for exporters in these sectors. The Government has also adopted a focused export-promotion and market-diversification strategy covering 40 priority countries. Sixteen Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), including the India–United Kingdom Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), are already in force. In addition, the FTA negotiations with the European Union have been successfully concluded, while India has signed an FTA with New Zealand. These agreements provide an opportunity for Indian textiles and apparel sector to enhance their exports and undertake market diversification. To further enhance textile sector competitiveness and export preparedness, the Ministry of Textiles has established six Textile Export Facilitation Centres (TEFCs), including at Ichalkaranji, Maharashtra, launched India Immersive Experience Programme through National Institute of Fashion Technology to showcase India's textiles, handicrafts, culture and design ecosystem to international institutions of designs/fashions. The Ministry of Textiles successfully concluded the Textiles Summit in June 2026 which brought together representatives from State Governments/ UTs, industry, and academia to foster collaborative dialogue on the growth of the textile sector and unlock the potential of districts. The products of textiles & handicraft were exported from more than 500 districts in 2025-26. The district led focused approach with 100 champion & 100 aspirational Textiles Districts has been adopted to facilitate better improved planning and implementation support . The third edition of Bharat Tex, a global mega textiles event was held from 14 th -17 th July, 2026 to showcase India's entire textile value chain, foster global business partnerships, and position India as a leading global sourcing and manufacturing hub for textiles and apparel. Collectively, these measures have helped diversify export markets, strengthen supply-chain resilience, improve market access including through e-commerce and enhance the competitiveness of Indian exporters, particularly MSMEs including Maharashtra. This information was provided by THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES SHRI PABITRA MARGHERITA in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today. **** MAM/VN (Rajya Sabha US Q797) (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288808) आगंतुक पटल  : 178 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Ministry of Textiles TRADE PREPAREDNESS AND EXPORT COMPETITIVENESS OF TEXTILE SECTOR प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: COTTON PRODUCTION
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles COTTON PRODUCTION प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 2:47PM by PIB Delhi Cotton production during the recent cotton seasons has ranged from 352.48 lakh bales in 2020-21 to 290.91 lakh bales (Provisional) in 2025-26. The variation in production is primarily attributable to changes in cotton acreage, as some farmers have diversified to other remunerative crops. Cotton productivity has, however, remained broadly stable in the range of 428-451 kg/hectare during this period. The details of area, production and productivity are given below. Cotton prices have reflected prevailing domestic and international market conditions. During the recent period, international cotton prices increased by about 19%, while domestic cotton prices (S-6 variety) increased by about 18%. To augment domestic availability, imports of raw cotton and cotton yarn are undertaken whenever required. The details of imports of raw cotton and cotton yarn are given below. The overall cotton availability in the country, including imports, meets the requirements of the domestic textile industry. The estimated production, carry-over stocks and imports meet the projected consumption and the cotton situation is continuously monitored. The Government has taken timely measures to support the textile industry, including exemption of the 11% import duty on cotton imports from 01.06.2026 to 31.10.2026 to facilitate adequate availability of raw cotton at competitive prices. The Government has also continued the exemption from import duty on Extra Long Staple (ELS) cotton (ITC HS Code 52010025), effective from 20.02.2024, to facilitate the availability of quality cotton for the textile industry. Further, the Government has approved the five-year Mission for Cotton Productivity (Kapas Kanti) (2026–27 to 2030–31), with an outlay of ₹5,659.22 crore to increase productivity & improve the quality of the cotton. title: Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, a package of six services are provided to eligible beneficiaries through Anganwadi Centres across the country
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, a package of six services are provided to eligible beneficiaries through Anganwadi Centres across the country Ministry has launched Pankhudi Portal to facilitate collaboration with organizations, individuals, corporates etc. for carrying out different activities under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, Mission Shakti and Mission Vatsalya प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 2:02PM by PIB Delhi In the 15 th Finance Commission, components of nutritional support for children below the age of 6 years, pregnant women and lactating mothers, Adolescent Girls (14 – 18 years); Early Childhood Care and Education [3-6 years]; Anganwadi infrastructure including modern, upgraded Saksham Anganwadi, Poshan Abhiyaan and Scheme for Adolescent Girls were reorganised under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0. Under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, a package of six services i.e., Supplementary Nutrition (SNP), Pre-school Non-formal Education, Nutrition & Health Education, Immunization, Health Check-up, and Referral Services are provided to the eligible beneficiaries through Anganwadi Centres across the country including State of Uttar Pradesh. Three of the six services, viz., Immunization, Health check-up and Referral Services are related to health and are provided through National Health Mission (NHM) & Public Health Infrastructure. These services are provided to the eligible registered beneficiaries i.e. children up to the age of 6 years, Pregnant Women and Lactating Mothers across the country and Adolescent Girls in the age group of 14 to 18 years in Aspirational Districts of States and all districts of North Eastern Region by through the platform of Anganwadi Centre. The district wise details of beneficiaries, infrastructure facilities, service delivery at Anganwadi Centres etc. across the country including state of Uttar Pradesh can be accessed from Poshan Tracker at https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics. Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and Anganwadi Helpers (AWHs) are honorary workers drawn from the local community who voluntarily come forward to render their services in the area of child care and development to help the local community for which they are paid honorarium. This honorarium is increased from time to time. From 1 st October, 2018, Government of India has enhanced the honorarium of AWWs at Anganwadi centres (AWCs) from Rs.3,000/- to Rs.4,500/- per month and AWHs from Rs.1,500/- to Rs.2,250/- per month as per the defined cost sharing ratio between the Centre and States and UTs. In addition, States and UTs are also paying additional monetary incentives and top ups to these functionaries from their own resources which vary from State to State. Besides, performance linked incentive of Rs.500/- per month is provided to AWWs and Rs.250/- per month to AWHs. The Ministry has introduced ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application as an important governance tool for real time monitoring and tracking of all Anganwadi Centres (AWCs), Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and beneficiaries on defined indicators under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0. Poshan Tracker app has enabled the Ministry to review the implementation of the scheme on various parameters and to make course correction. It has facilitated near real time data collection for Anganwadi Services such as, opening of AWCs, daily attendance of children, ECCE activities, Growth Monitoring of children, Provision of Hot Cooked Meal (HCM) and Take-Home Ration (THR), Growth Measurement etc. This Mission is a universal umbrella scheme where there are no entry barriers for any beneficiary to register and receive services. Every beneficiary who is willing to undergo the eKYC procedure for Facial Recognition System (FRS), is fully entitled to receive the benefits of the scheme. This Aadhaar based tracking has enabled proper identification of beneficiaries, prevention of leakages and eliminating ghost entries. As per the data available on the Poshan Tracker dashboard, 99.88% registered beneficiaries are Aadhaar verified. For last mile tracking of Service Delivery, Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) has developed Facial Recognition System (FRS) in Poshan Tracker Application for distribution of Take-Home Ration (THR) to ensure that benefit is given only to the intended beneficiary registered in Poshan Tracker. The Nominee Module has also been introduced in Poshan Tracker to ensure uninterrupted delivery of Take-Home Ration (THR) to the beneficiaries. If due to any reason, the registered beneficiary is unable to visit the Anganwadi Centre to receive their THR through FRS, she can choose a nominee on her behalf to receive her THR. Nominee has to undergo e-KYC only ONCE, but face matching will be done every time for receiving THR on behalf of the beneficiary. Even after addition of the nominee, beneficiary can still continue to receive THR, if they so wish to. This has improved ease of living for the beneficiaries. Ministry has launched Pankhudi Portal to facilitate collaboration with organizations, individuals, corporates etc for carrying out different activities under the three Missions namely Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0, Mission Shakti and Mission Vatsalya. Details are available on the link https://pankhudi.wcd.gov.in/web/home. This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
title: Ministry of Women and Child Development launched Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 to improve nutritional outcomes among children from 0-6 years
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development Ministry of Women and Child Development launched Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 to improve nutritional outcomes among children from 0-6 years Ministry introduced ‘Poshan Tracker’ application as an important governance tool Ministry of Women & Child Development and Ministry of Health & Family Welfare have jointly released Protocol for Management of Malnutrition in Children प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 2:01PM by PIB Delhi To improve nutritional outcomes among the children from 0-6 years of age, Ministry of Women and Child Development has launched Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0) by subsuming Anganwadi services, Poshan Abhiyaan and Scheme for Adolescent girls (14-18 years, in Aspirational Districts and North-Eastern region). It is a Centrally Sponsored Mission, where the responsibility for implementation of various activities lies with the States and UTs. This Mission includes beneficiaries; children under 6 years of age, pregnant women, lactating mothers and adolescent girls (14-18 years, in Northeastern States and Aspirational Districts) of the country. The Ministry introduced ‘Poshan Tracker’ application as an important governance tool in March 2021 for monitoring and tracking of all Anganwadi Centres (AWCs), Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and beneficiaries on defined indicators under Mission Poshan 2.0. It has facilitated near real time data collection for Anganwadi Services such as, opening of AWCs, daily attendance of children, ECCE activities, Growth Monitoring of children, distribution of Hot Cooked Meal (HCM) and Take-Home Ration (THR) etc. Poshan Tracker application has enabled to review the implementation of the scheme on various parameters and to make course correction. For last mile tracking of service delivery, Facial Recognition System (FRS) has been introduced in Poshan Tracker app for distribution of Take-Home Ration to ensure that beneﬁt is given only to the intended beneﬁciary registered in Poshan Tracker. The details of the nutritional indicators, children benefited and progress of the scheme in all States and UTs, including Shahjahanpur constituency are available at Poshan Tracker dashboard: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics. Under Mission Poshan 2.0 a new strategy has been made for reduction in malnutrition and for improved health, wellness and immunity through activities like community engagement, outreach, behavioural change and advocacy. It focuses on Maternal Nutrition, Infant and Young Child Feeding Norms, treatment of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM)/ Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) and wellness through AYUSH practices to reduce prevalence of wasting, stunting, anaemia and being underweight. Under this Mission, Supplementary Nutrition is provided to Children (6 months to 6 years), Pregnant Women, Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls in accordance with the nutrition norms contained in Schedule-II of the National Food Security Act, 2013. These norms have been revised in January 2023. The old norms were largely calorie-specific; however, the revised norms are more comprehensive and balanced in terms of both quantity and quality of supplementary nutrition based on the principles of diet diversity that provides for quality protein, healthy fats and micronutrients (Calcium, Zinc, Iron, Dietary Folate, Vitamin A, Vitamin-B6 and Vitamin B-12 ). Extra Supplementary Nutrition in the form of Take-Home Ration (THR) is provided to Severely Acutely Malnourished (SAM) children. Also, Ministry of Women & Child Development and Ministry of Health & Family Welfare have jointly released the Protocol for Management of Malnutrition in Children to prevent and treat severely acute malnutrition in children and for reducing associated morbidity and mortality. The community-based approach involves timely detection and screening of children with severe acute malnutrition in the community, management for those without medical complications with wholesome, local nutritious foods at home and supportive medical care. Under this Mission, one of the major activities undertaken is Community Mobilization and Awareness Advocacy to educate people on nutritional aspects as adoption of good nutrition habit requires sustained efforts for behavioural change. State and UTs are conducting and reporting regular sensitisation activities under Jan Andolans during Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada celebrated in the months of September and March-April respectively. Community Based Events (CBEs) have served as a significant strategy in changing nutritional practices and all Anganwadi workers are required to conduct two Community Based Events every month. This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. Savitri Thakur in Lok Sabha in reply to a question. ***** SS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288797) आगंतुक पटल  : 241 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Kannada , Tamil , Bengali , Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Women and Child Development Ministry of Women and Child Development launched Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 to improve nutritional outcomes among children from 0-6 years Ministry introduced ‘Poshan Tracker’ application as an important governance tool Ministry of Women & Child Development and Ministry of Health & Family Welfare have jointly released Protocol for Management of Malnutrition in Children प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
title: Two lakh Anganwadi Centres have been approved to be upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis for delivery of improved nutrition and for ECCE activities
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development Two lakh Anganwadi Centres have been approved to be upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis for delivery of improved nutrition and for ECCE activities प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 2:00PM by PIB Delhi To address the challenges of malnutrition, Anganwadi services, Poshan Abhiyaan and Scheme for Adolescent girls have been subsumed under the umbrella Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0). It is a Centrally Sponsored Mission, where the responsibility for implementation of various activities lies with the States and UTs. The Mission is being implemented in all States and UTs in the country including high burden districts. The Mission includes beneficiaries; Children under 6 years of age, pregnant women, lactating mothers and adolescent girls (age 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and North-Eastern region). Under the Mission, two lakh Anganwadi Centres (AWCs) have been approved to be upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis for delivery of improved nutrition and for ECCE activities. These AWCs are equipped with better infrastructure such as LED screens, water filtration system, Poshan Vatika, Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) material and Building as Learning Aid (BaLA) paintings. Further, Supplementary Nutrition is provided to Children (6 months to 6 years), Pregnant Women, Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls in accordance with the nutrition norms contained in Schedule-II of the National Food Security Act, 2013. These norms have been revised in January 2023. The old norms were largely calorie-specific; however, the revised norms are more comprehensive and balanced in terms of both quantity and quality of supplementary nutrition based on the principles of diet diversity. Extra Supplementary Nutrition (Take Home Ration) is also provided to Severely Acute Malnourished (SAM) children. The Scheme is digitally monitored and regularly reviewed by the Ministry using ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application, an ICT based governance tool. The application enables near real time entry of data and tracking of all activities in the Anganwadi Centers (AWC), Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and beneficiaries on defined indicators. State-wise details of the beneficiaries identified along with the improvements achieved is available at the given link of Poshan Tracker: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics. Ministry of Women & Child Development and Ministry of Health & Family Welfare have jointly released the Protocol for Management of Malnutrition in Children to prevent and treat severely acute malnutrition in children and for reducing associated morbidity and mortality. The community-based approach involves timely detection and screening of children with severe acute malnutrition in the community, management for those without medical complications with wholesome, local nutritious foods at home and supportive medical care. Under this Mission, one of the major activities undertaken is Community Mobilization and Awareness Advocacy to educate people on nutritional aspects as adoption of good nutrition habit requires sustained efforts for behavioural change. State and UTs are conducting and reporting regular sensitisation activities under Jan Andolans during Poshan Maah and Poshan Pakhwada celebrated in the months of September and March-April, respectively. Community Based Events (CBEs) have served as a significant strategy in changing nutritional practices and all Anganwadi workers are required to conduct two Community Based Events every month. A third-party evaluation and impact assessment of Poshan Abhiyaan was conducted by NITI Aayog in 2020 and has found its relevance to be satisfactory for tackling malnutrition in the country. NITI Aayog has also got conducted outcome-based evaluation of Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 in 2025. Evidence from institutional assessments and household surveys indicated that in its current form, Mission Poshan 2.0 represents the Government’s latest effort to holistically combat malnutrition and promote child development, by building on past programs with a converged and strengthened approach. Further, on the micronutrient front, the prevalence of anaemia among children aged 6–59 months declined by 8.5 percentage points, reflecting the potential impact of iron-folic acid supplementation, fortified foods, and improved outreach under SNP and related interventions. This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. Savitri Thakur in Lok Sabha in reply to a question. ***** SS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288795) आगंतुक पटल  : 149 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Tamil , Urdu , हिन्दी , Telugu Ministry of Women and Child Development Two lakh Anganwadi Centres have been approved to be upgraded as Saksham Anganwadis for delivery of improved nutrition and for ECCE activities प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
title: Significant measures taken by the Ministry of Women and Child Development to improve nutritional outcomes under Mission Poshan 2.0
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development Significant measures taken by the Ministry of Women and Child Development to improve nutritional outcomes under Mission Poshan 2.0 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 1:59PM by PIB Delhi To address the challenges of malnutrition, Anganwadi services, Poshan Abhiyaan and Scheme for Adolescent girls (of 14-18 years in Aspirational Districts and North-Eastern region) have been subsumed under the umbrella Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 (Mission Poshan 2.0). It is a Centrally Sponsored mission, where the responsibility for implementation of various activities lies with the States and UTs. The Mission is being implemented in all States and UTs in the country. Rs. 21,960 crores have been allocated under the Mission Poshan 2.0 in Financial Year 2025-26. The Ministry of Women and Child Development (MoWCD) has launched ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application, an ICT based tool, for monitoring and tracking of all activities related to Anganwadi Centres (AWCs), Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and beneficiaries on defined indicators under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0. Technology under Poshan Tracker is being leveraged for dynamic identification of stunting, wasting, under-weight prevalence among children under 5 years of age. The State wise information on nutrition indicators in the country is available on the Poshan Tracker public dashboard at the given link: https://www.poshantracker.in/statistics. As per the Cause of Death Report (2021-23) released by Sample Registration System-Registrar General of India (SRS-RGI), malnutrition is not identified as a direct cause of death in children; however, it can increase morbidity and mortality by reducing resistance to infections. Under the Mission Poshan 2.0, significant measures have been taken by the MoWCD to improve nutritional outcomes: Supplementary Nutrition is provided to Children (6 months to 6 years), Pregnant Women, Lactating Mothers and Adolescent Girls in accordance with the nutrition norms contained in Schedule-II of the National Food Security Act, 2013. Additional Nutrition is also provided to Severely Acute Malnourished (SAM) children in form of Take-Home Ration (THR). title: One Stop Centre provides integrated and immediate support and assistance under one roof to women affected by violence and those in distress
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development One Stop Centre provides integrated and immediate support and assistance under one roof to women affected by violence and those in distress OSCs integrated with Women Helpline to strengthen convergence and ensure seamless access to support services OSCs also integrated with Shakti Sadan to enable referral of women requiring long-term institutional support, rehabilitation and safe accommodation प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 1:58PM by PIB Delhi One Stop Centre (OSC) is a component of the Sambal vertical under the umbrella Mission Shakti. It provides integrated and immediate support and assistance under one roof to women affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and public spaces all across the country. So far, 1,033 One Stop Centres (OSCs) have been approved across the country. Out of which, 985 One Stop Centres have been made operational across the country and since inception, i.e. 1st April, 2015 to 30 th June, 2026, over 15.20 lakh women have been assisted in the country. The Central Government provides 100% financial assistance to States/ UTs for appointment/hiring 13 manpower resources including 1 Centre Administrator, 2 Case Workers, 1 Psycho-social Counsellor, 1 Para Legal Personnel/ Lawyer, 1 Para Medical Personnel at each OSC with a provision of flexibility in the staffing composition based on local needs and operational feasibility. The overall implementation of the OSC scheme lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations. To strengthen convergence and ensure seamless access to support services, OSCs have been integrated with the Women Helpline (WHL), and so far, 657 OSCs have been integrated. Through this integration, women can be referred to appropriate services in a timely and coordinated manner. Further, the Women Helpline has been integrated with the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS-112), Child Helpline (1098) and other relevant service delivery mechanisms to facilitate prompt emergency response and effective inter-agency coordination. In addition, OSCs have also been integrated with Shakti Sadan to enable referral of women requiring long-term institutional support, rehabilitation and safe accommodation, thereby ensuring a continuum of care under the Mission Shakti framework. Under the overarching ‘Mission Shakti’, erstwhile schemes of ‘Swadhar Greh’ – Home for women in difficult circumstances and ‘Ujjawala’- Home for women rescued from Trafficking, have been merged and are now known as ‘Shakti Sadan Scheme’, which is an Integrated Relief and Rehabilitation Home for women in distressful situations including trafficked women. It aims at creating a safe and enabling environment for the women in such difficult situations, to enable them to overcome the adverse circumstances. Under Shakti Sadan Scheme, the residents of Shakti Sadan are provided with shelter, food, clothing, counselling, primary health facilities and other daily requirements. The residents also to be provided vocational training, facility for opening of bank accounts, social security benefits etc. in convergence with the relevant departments. Further, arrangement is made by the implementing organization for providing vocational training/ skill development classes to the women through the Vocational Training Institutes recognized by the Directorate General of Employment and Training under the Ministry of Labour and Employment/ Training Partners of National Skill Development Council (NSDC). Training and examination fee, if not provided under any other scheme/ programmes of the Central/ State Government, would be reimbursed on submission of the certificate issued by the vocational training institute on successful completion of training. Micro Credit will be facilitated through SIDBI, Mudra and other relevant schemes of Central/State government in case residents want to start small-scale industry/ business. Further, Sakhi Niwas Scheme (Working Women Hostel) under the overarching Mission Shakti, aims to promote availability of safe and conveniently located accommodation for working women in urban, semi-urban and also in rural areas where employment opportunity for women exists. Under the Scheme, financial assistance is provided for running of Sakhi Niwas in rented premises for working women and for those women who are under training for job. Provision of Day Care Centre for children of the residents of the Sakhi Niwas is an important aspect of the scheme. Presently, 575 Sakhi Niwas are functional across the country. This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. title: ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application is an important governance tool for real time monitoring and tracking under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application is an important governance tool for real time monitoring and tracking under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 Nominee Module has also been introduced in Poshan Tracker to ensure uninterrupted delivery of Take-Home Ration to beneficiaries प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 1:57PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry has introduced ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application as an important governance tool for real time monitoring and tracking of all Anganwadi Centres (AWCs), Anganwadi Workers (AWWs) and beneficiaries on defined indicators under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0. Poshan Tracker app has enabled the Ministry to review the implementation of the scheme on various parameters and to make course correction. It has facilitated near real time data collection for Anganwadi Services such as, opening of AWCs, daily attendance of children, ECCE activities, Growth Monitoring of children, Provision of Hot Cooked Meal (HCM) and Take-Home Ration (THR), Growth Measurement etc. This Mission is a universal umbrella scheme where there are no entry barriers for any beneficiary to register and receive services. Every beneficiary who is willing to undergo the e-KYC procedure for Facial Recognition System (FRS), is fully entitled to receive the benefits of the scheme. This Aadhaar based tracking has enabled proper identification of beneficiaries, prevention of leakages and eliminating ghost entries. As per the data available on the Poshan Tracker dashboard, 99.88% registered beneficiaries are Aadhaar verified. For last mile tracking of Service Delivery, Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) has developed Facial Recognition System (FRS) in Poshan Tracker Application for distribution of Take-Home Ration (THR) to ensure that benefit is given only to the intended beneficiary registered in Poshan Tracker. The Nominee Module has also been introduced in Poshan Tracker to ensure uninterrupted delivery of Take-Home Ration (THR) to the beneficiaries. If due to any reason, the registered beneficiary is unable to visit the Anganwadi Centre to receive their THR through FRS, she can choose a nominee on her behalf to receive her THR. Nominee has to undergo e-KYC only ONCE, but face matching will be done every time for receiving THR on behalf of the beneficiary. Even after addition of the nominee, beneficiary can still continue to receive THR, if they so wish to. This has improved ease of living for the beneficiaries. The Ministry releases funds to all States and UTs for procurement of Smart Phones to Anganwadi Workers (AWWs), Lady Supervisors and Block Coordinators for registration, data entry, tracking and monitoring of all beneficiaries in the Poshan Tracker application. Funds for Growth Monitoring Devices (Infantometer and Stadiometer for length and height measurement, Weighing Scale-Infant and Weighing Scale-Mother & Child for weight measurement of the beneficiaries) are also released to all the States and UTs. An amount of ₹10,000+ GST per Smart phone and ₹8,000/- for a set of 4 GMDs is provided by the Central Government on cost-sharing basis. Outcome-based assessment and continuous monitoring are being carried out through system-generated analytics of the Poshan Tracker to evaluate the impact of digitalization on nutrition monitoring, ECCE delivery, beneficiary verification, and service efficiency. Digital learning support has been strengthened by integrating ECCE content aligned with the Navchetana (National Framework of Early Childhood Stimulation) and Aadharshila (National Curriculum for Early Childhood Care and Education) on the Poshan Tracker in the form of videos, activity modules, and home-based learning materials. The application currently hosts 249 ECCE videos, 190 audio messages, and over 130 activity-based learning resources. For children in the 0–3 years age group, 140 home-based activities through 14 videos have been developed in the light of Navchetana framework, to support structured home visits and promote caregiver engagement for early childhood stimulation. These initiatives have contributed to improved uniformity, quality, and effectiveness of Early Childhood Education and Care (ECCE) at Anganwadi Centres. The beneficiary interface further enables dissemination of learning content and messages to parents on ECCE, early stimulation, and childcare practices, thereby strengthening caregiver awareness and community participation in early childhood development. An outcome-based evaluation study of Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 was conducted by Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO), NITI Aayog (2025). As per the study, evidence from institutional assessments and household surveys indicates that digitalization through Poshan Tracker Application has a multi-dimensional impact on nutrition monitoring, Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE), beneficiary authentication, and service delivery efficiency. The Report also highlighted Poshan Tracker as a significant shift from manual, paper-based systems to a technology-enabled governance framework under the Supplementary Nutrition Programme (SNP). As per the report Poshan Tracker, introduced by MoWCD, has become the cornerstone for digital monitoring of beneficiaries, inventory, and service delivery at Anganwadi Centres (AWCs). This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. Savitri Thakur in Lok Sabha in reply to a question. ***** SS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288793) आगंतुक पटल  : 187 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil , Kannada Ministry of Women and Child Development ‘Poshan Tracker’ digital application is an important governance tool for real time monitoring and tracking under Mission Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0 Nominee Module has also been introduced in Poshan Tracker to ensure uninterrupted delivery of Take-Home Ration to beneficiaries प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: ENGINEERING SERVICES (MAIN) EXAMINATION, 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau UPSC ENGINEERING SERVICES (MAIN) EXAMINATION, 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 7:01PM by PIB Delhi On the basis of the result of the written part of the Engineering Services (Main) Examination, 2026 held by U.P.S.C. on 21 st June 2026, the candidates with the under mentioned Roll Numbers have qualified for Interview/ Personality Test. 2. The candidature of these candidates is PROVISIONAL subject to their being found eligible in all respects. The candidates would be required to produce the original certificates/documents in support of their claims relating to age, educational qualifications, community, benchmark disability (where applicable) etc. at the time of the Personality Test. They are, therefore, advised to keep their certificates/documents ready before appearance in the Personality Test and check beforehand the requirement of certificates in accordance with the Important Instructions, which are available on the website of the Commission. 3.1 The Commission shall provide a window of 15 (Fifteen) days soon after the declaration of result of Main/Stage-II part of Engineering Services Examination, 2026 to the candidates who qualified for Personality Test/Interview. The candidates, as per Note 2 below Rule 6 of the Rules of Engineering Services Examination, 2026, shall be required to update their details and to upload the proof of passing of the requisite qualifying examination at the specified module/portal, failing which such candidates will not be allowed to appear in the Personality Test/Interview and his/her candidature will be liable to be cancelled. The candidates are advised to check the Commission’s website regularly for this purpose. 3.2 In this period, all the candidates qualified for Personality Test shall also be provided an option to update Correspondence/Postal Address, Higher Qualification, Achievement in different fields, Employment Details/Service Experience, Service Allocation, Service Preferences. The details updated in this window will be treated as final and no request for any change in these fields received through any other mode will be entertained. 3.3 It may be noted that all the candidates qualified for Personality Test/Interview will have to mandatorily login to the portal during this window and update and/or reconfirm their details etc. and submit the Application Form to enable the Commission to generate e-summon letter, failing which such candidates will not be allowed to participate in the further stage of examination. Candidates who have uploaded the required documents/information earlier and have no information to update/fill in are also required to mandatorily login and finally submit after verifying the details so as to generate the e-summon letter for Personality Test of ESE-2026. 4. The instructions for updating the Application Form and the Rules of the Engineering Services Examination, 2026, must be read carefully with regard to the certificates that will be produced at the time of Interview. The candidate will be solely responsible for not producing sufficient proof in support of his/her age, date of birth, educational qualification, community (SC/ST/OBC/EWS), and Certificate of Disability (in the case of PwBD candidate).  In case any of the written qualified candidate fails to bring any or all the required original documents in support of his/her candidature for the Engineering Services Examination, 2026, he/she will not be allowed to present himself/herself before the PT Board and no TA will be allowed. 5. The schedule of the Personality Test (Interview) will be informed to the candidates in due course.  The exact date of interview will, however, be intimated to the candidates through e-Summon Letter, which may be downloaded from the Commission’s websites https://www.upsc.gov.in and https://www.upsconline.gov.in . A Roll Number-wise Interview Schedule will also be made available on the Commission’s website. The candidates are requested to visit the Commission’s website for updates in this regard. 6. No request for change in the date and time of the Personality Test intimated to the candidates will be entertained under any circumstances. 7. The marks-sheet of all candidates (Qualified & Non-Qualified), will be uploaded on the Commission’s Website after the publication of the final result (i.e. after the conduct of Personality Test) and will remain available on the website for a period of 30 days. 8. The candidates can access the marks-sheets after keying their Roll Numbers and Date of Birth.  The authenticated copy of the marks-sheet would, however, be issued by the UPSC to candidates based on specific request accompanied by a self-addressed stamped envelope. The candidates desirous of obtaining printed/hard copies of the marks sheets should make the request within 30 days of the display of the marks on the Commission’s website, beyond which such requests would not be entertained. 9. The candidates may obtain any information/clarification regarding their issue(s) (if any) in respect of the above mentioned Examination on Tel. No. 011- 40303444/24041001 of the Commission’s Call Centre from 09:00 AM to 08:00 PM. MOBILE PHONES ARE BANNED IN THE CAMPUS OF UPSC EXAMINATION HALLS. The candidature of these candidates is PROVISIONAL subject to their being found eligible in all respects. The candidates would be required to produce the original certificates/documents in support of their claims relating to age, educational qualifications, community, benchmark disability (where applicable) etc. at the time of the Personality Test. They are, therefore, advised to keep their certificates/documents ready before appearance in the Personality Test and check beforehand the requirement of certificates in accordance with the Important Instructions, which are available on the website of the Commission. 3.1 The Commission shall provide a window of 15 (Fifteen) days soon after the declaration of result of Main/Stage-II part of Engineering Services Examination, 2026 to the candidates who qualified for Personality Test/Interview. title: Kargil Vijay Diwas 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder Kargil Vijay Diwas 2026 A Tribute to Valour, Sacrifice, and the Spirit of India प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                24 JUL 2026 3:50PM by PIB Delhi Kargil Vijay Diwas honours the courage, sacrifice, and unwavering resolve of the Bravehearts of Operation Vijay. It commemorates India's historic victory in the Kargil War and celebrates the spirit that safeguarded the Nation's sovereignty. The occasion also reflects Kargil's enduring legacy. It continues to strengthen India's military preparedness, inspire generations, and reinforce the Nation's unwavering commitment to its security. When Courage Conquered the Peaks The Kargil War stands among the greatest chapters in India's military history. It reflects unmatched bravery, grit, and determination. It remains a lasting symbol of national pride and inspiration. This year, the nation marks the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas with gratitude and reverence. It commemorates India's historic victory in 1999. Indian soldiers reclaimed the snow-covered heights of Kargil through extraordinary courage and unwavering resolve. On 26 July, the Tricolour once again flew proudly over the rugged mountains of Ladakh. It became a timeless symbol of sacrifice, valour, and India's unbreakable spirit. The Kargil conflict began in May 1999. Intruders crossed the Line of Control and occupied Indian positions on commanding heights. Their aim was to cut the link between Kashmir and Ladakh. The larger objective was to force India into negotiations on the Kashmir dispute. But they underestimated the will of a nation.  India responded with Operation Vijay. The mission reflected meticulous planning, unwavering determination, and the indomitable spirit of Indian soldiers. After more than two months of intense fighting, every intruder was driven out. Every occupied position returned to Indian control. Kargil Vijay Diwas honours every Braveheart who sacrificed everything for the motherland. Their sacrifice strengthened India's resolve to secure every inch of its territory. The conflict reshaped the nation's military preparedness and defence outlook for the years ahead. Its lessons continue to guide India's march towards a stronger and more self-reliant future. It reminds every Indian that courage, sacrifice, unity, and sovereignty will forever remain the nation's greatest strength. The Road to Operation Vijay The Kargil War began in the summer of 1999, soon after the Lahore Declaration. While much of India endured scorching heat, fierce battles unfolded across the icy heights of Kargil. Pakistani forces infiltrated Indian territory and occupied winter vacated posts on commanding ridges. The conflict tested courage, endurance, and sacrifice in one of the world's harshest battlefields. It remains the only conventional war fought between two nuclear armed nations. The Infiltration The intrusion was part of Pakistan's Operation Badr. Pakistani forces, disguised as Kashmiri terrorists, crossed the Line of Control and occupied Indian positions. Their aim was to cut the link between Kashmir and Ladakh. They also sought to isolate Indian Army troops on the Siachen Glacier. The larger objective was to force India into negotiations on the Kashmir dispute. On 3 May 1999, local residents first reported suspicious movement in the Kargil sector. Reconnaissance patrols were immediately dispatched to verify the reports. Extensive patrolling and aerial surveillance soon revealed the scale of the occupation. The infiltrators had entrenched themselves on dominating heights overlooking the Srinagar to Leh Highway. Many positions stood above 5,000 metres, making every military operation exceptionally challenging. Operation Vijay Begins India responded with restraint, resolve, and determination. The government directed that the Line of Control would not be crossed. The mission was clear. Every occupied post had to be reclaimed. The Indian Army launched Operation Vijay to evict the intruders. The Indian Air Force joined the campaign through Operation Safed Sagar on 26 May 1999. The Indian Navy also deployed in full strength, demonstrating India's resolve across every domain. Together, the three Services executed a coordinated campaign. Operation Vijay followed the strategy of contain, evict, and deny. Priority was given to recapturing the heights dominating the Srinagar to Leh Highway. Additional troops, artillery, engineers, specialised equipment, and logistics were rapidly inducted. Soldiers climbed near vertical cliffs under relentless enemy fire. They battled freezing temperatures, thin air, and unforgiving terrain. Battles That Changed the Course of the War The Battle of Tololing marked one of the first major breakthroughs of the campaign. Indian troops launched their assault in the last week of May 1999. Point 4590 and Tololing was fully recaptured on 13 June, opening the way for further advances. The Battle of Tiger Hill became one of the defining moments of the war. Tiger Hill was among the highest peaks in the Dras sector and one of the Indian Army's most important objectives. After a daring assault, the peak was recaptured on 4 July 1999, significantly shifting the momentum in India's favour. Fierce fighting also took place at Point 4875, Batalik, Mushkoh Valley, and Kaksar. Indian soldiers fought peak by peak to reclaim every occupied position. After nearly three months of relentless operations, every occupied Indian post was recaptured. India secured victory without crossing the Line of Control, earning global respect for its restraint, professionalism, and unwavering resolve. A Victory That Inspired a Nation The Kargil War became a defining chapter in India's history. It showcased the extraordinary courage of Indian soldiers and united the nation in pride. On 14 July 1999 , then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee addressed the nation and declared Operation Vijay a success. He paid tribute to the courage, sacrifice, and unwavering resolve of the Armed Forces. The victory reaffirmed that every inch of Indian territory would be defended at any cost. It strengthened the nation's faith in its Armed Forces and inspired generations of Indians. The Bravery That Defined Kargil The victory in Kargil was made possible by countless acts of courage. Every peak reclaimed reflected the determination and sacrifice of India's Armed Forces. While every soldier contributed to Operation Vijay, several acts of exceptional gallantry became defining moments of the conflict. Heroes such as Grenadier Yogendra Singh Yadav, Captain Vikram Batra, Captain Vijyant Thapar, and many others became symbols of courage and selfless service. The nation honoured this extraordinary valour with its highest military decorations. 4 soldiers were awarded the Param Vir Chakra , India's highest gallantry award. 9 received the Maha Vir Chakra , while 55 were honoured with the Vir Chakra . 1 soldier was conferred the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal . 6 received the Uttam Yudh Seva Medal , and 8 were awarded the Yudh Seva Medal . The Sena Medal was awarded to 83 personnel, while 24 received the Vayu Sena Medal. These honours reflect the extraordinary courage, leadership, and sacrifice displayed during the Kargil War. Read the inspiring stories of these Bravehearts Click To Read More Here. From Battlefield Lessons to a Stronger Defence Ecosystem The Kargil War became a turning point in India's defence journey. It highlighted the need for stronger coordination, faster modernisation, and greater self-reliance. Over the years, India has undertaken wide ranging reforms to strengthen its defence ecosystem and build indigenous capabilities. Today, these efforts are shaping a stronger, more capable, and increasingly Atmanirbhar military. Some of the key reforms and initiatives are outlined below: Establishment of the Department of Military Affairs The Department of Military Affairs was created as a part of Higher Defence Management Reforms. It functions under the CDS, who serves as its Secretary. The department promotes jointmanship among the Army, Navy, and Air Force. It also supports coordinated defence doctrines, planning, and procedures across the three Services. Creation of the Chief of Defence Staff One of the most significant reforms was the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff (CDS). The CDS serves as the single point military adviser to the Government. The role also promotes greater jointness among the Army, Navy, and Air Force. General Bipin Rawat became India's first CDS in 2020. The post is currently held by General N. S. Raja Subramani. Foreign Direct Investment in Defence The defence industry was opened to private sector participation. The FDI limit has increased to 74 per cent through the Automatic Route for new defence industrial licences. It also allows up to 100 per cent through the Government Route where modern technology is introduced. As of March 2026, the sector has attracted FDI worth ₹6,670.59 crore. The Government also promotes co-development and co-production with Foreign Original Equipment Manufacturers to strengthen advanced defence manufacturing. Enhanced Defence Budget India's defence allocation has risen steadily from ₹2.53 lakh crore in 2013–14 to ₹7.85 lakh crore in 2026–27. Capital expenditure has also increased from ₹94,587.95 crore in 2014–15 to ₹2.19 lakh crore in 2026–27. These investments are strengthening long term military capability through modern equipment, infrastructure, and strategic assets. Growth in Defence Production and Exports India's defence production reached an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in 2025–26, almost four times higher than ₹46,429 crore in 2014–15. Defence exports increased from ₹686 crore in 2013–14 to ₹38,424 crore in 2025–26, a rise of more than 56 times. Today, Indian defence products are exported to over 80 countries . Driven by Make in India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat, India is steadily emerging as a defence manufacturing nation. Nearly 65 per cent of defence equipment is now produced within the country, compared to an earlier import dependence of 65 to 70 per cent. Accelerating Indigenous Defence Manufacturing The Ministry of Defence launched the Srijan Defence Portal . The portal connects Defence Public Sector Undertakings and Service Headquarters with industries, MSMEs, and startups for indigenisation. Positive Indigenisation Lists were introduced in 2021 under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiative. Till May 2026, five Positive Indigenisation Lists covering 5,012 items of DPSUs have been notified. More than 15,700 defence items, including 3,204 Positive Indigenisation List items, have been indigenised during the last five years. DPSUs have placed domestic orders worth ₹9,782 crore, strengthening MSMEs, startups, research institutions, and India's defence manufacturing ecosystem. Defence Industrial Corridors Driving Regional Manufacturing Defence Industrial Corridors have emerged as key growth centres for defence manufacturing, strengthening regional supply chains and fostering integrated industrial ecosystems. By April 2026, the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor had attracted investment commitments worth ₹ 42,057 crore, with grounded investments of ₹ 4,409 crore, supported by the establishment of the Defence Technology & Test Centre (DTTC) to enhance testing and innovation capabilities. During the same period, the Tamil Nadu Defence Industrial Corridor attracted investments worth ₹ 32,699 crore, with actual investments reaching ₹ 6,446 crore. Together, these corridors are accelerating industrial infrastructure development, expanding domestic manufacturing capacity, and generating new employment opportunities. Agnipath Scheme The Agnipath Scheme was launched to recruit young men and women into the Armed Forces as Agniveers for a four-year service period. The scheme aims to create a youthful, tech-savvy, and combat-ready military force with a modern outlook. Agniveers receive military training, specialised skill development, and educational opportunities through partnerships with institutions such as IGNOU and NIOS. The scheme also provides nationally recognised skill certificates and career pathways after service. The legacy of Kargil continues to inspire reforms that are strengthening India's Armed Forces and reinforcing the nation's security. Towards a Future Ready Military The character of warfare has changed significantly since the Kargil War. Modern conflicts demand advanced technology, superior firepower, and rapid decision making. India has strengthened its military capabilities through the induction of modern platforms and the development of next generation defence technologies. These capabilities are enhancing operational readiness across land, air, sea, space, and emerging domains. Some of the key platforms and emerging technologies driving this transformation are outlined below. Modern Platforms in Service India has inducted advanced platforms across the three Services to strengthen combat capability and enhance operational effectiveness. Arjun Mk IA Battle Tank: The Arjun Mk IA battle tank was inducted into the Indian Army in February 2021. It strengthened India's indigenous armoured capability. INS Vikrant: India's first indigenous aircraft carrier, INS Vikrant, was commissioned on 2 September 2022. It marked a major milestone in maritime capability and self-reliance. Rafale Fighter Aircraft: By 2030, India will operate 62 Rafale fighter aircraft, including 26 Rafale M aircraft. India will become the first country after France to operate both variants. Apache and Chinook Helicopters: The induction of Apache attack helicopters and Chinook heavy lift helicopters has enhanced combat capability and strategic airlift capacity. Integration of Drone Warfare: India has integrated drone warfare into its military doctrine. Drones now strengthen surveillance, reconnaissance, precision operations, and battlefield effectiveness. BrahMos Cruise Missile: The first successful BrahMos launch took place on 12 June 2001. This multi-platform supersonic cruise missile can be launched from land, sea, and air. It has a range of up to 290 kilometres and travels at nearly Mach 2.8. Project 17A Stealth Frigates: Project 17A is the Indian Navy's advanced stealth frigate programme to build seven next generation guided missile warships. These frigates are designed for anti-air, anti-surface, and anti-submarine warfare. Sandhayak Class Survey Vessels: The Sandhayak class survey vessels strengthen the Indian Navy's hydrographic capability by mapping the seabed and coastal waters. The indigenous class comprises INS Sandhayak, INS Nirdeshak, INS Ikshak, and INS Sanshodhak, enhancing India's maritime survey and navigation capabilities. Arnala Class Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft: The Arnala class strengthens the Indian Navy's coastal defence and anti-submarine warfare capability. The indigenous eight ship class comprises INS Arnala, INS Androth, INS Anjadip, INS Amini, INS Abhay, INS Agray, INS Akshay, and the recently commissioned INS Ajay. INS Arnala is the largest waterjet propelled warship inducted into the Indian Navy. Click To Read More: Guardians of India's Maritime Frontiers Emerging Technologies and Strategic Capabilities India is investing in advanced technologies to prepare its Armed Forces for the battlefields of tomorrow. Mission Shakti: On 27 March 2019, India successfully conducted Mission Shakti, an anti-satellite missile test, from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island. With this achievement, India joined the exclusive group of nations possessing anti-satellite capability. Artificial Intelligence in Defence: In 2022, India introduced 75 Artificial Intelligence based technologies for surveillance, cyber security, logistics, autonomous systems, and battlefield support. Mission Divyastra: On 11 March 2024, India successfully tested a long range missile carrying multiple warheads against different targets under Mission Divyastra. Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket: The maiden flight test of the Pinaka Long Range Guided Rocket was successfully conducted on 29 December 2025. The rocket demonstrated a maximum range of 120 kilometres and achieved textbook precision during the trial. Advanced Air Defence System: On 23 August 2025, DRDO successfully tested an advanced air defence system. It combines missile interceptors, short range air defence weapons, and laser based technologies. Hypersonic Missile Technologies: India has advanced next generation propulsion systems for hypersonic missiles. In January 2026, DRDO completed a successful long duration scramjet combustor ground test. A new Hypersonic Wind Tunnel in Hyderabad now supports future high speed missile development. Kusha Long Range Surface to Air Missile: In July 2026, DRDO successfully conducted the maiden flight test of the Kusha missile. It intercepted a simulated high speed aerial threat. The system can neutralise fighter jets, missiles, unmanned aerial vehicles, and large enemy aircraft across a wide range and altitude. It has been developed indigenously by DRDO laboratories and industry partners. Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile: In June 2026, DRDO successfully flight tested the Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island. The missile successfully achieved all test objectives. It is an indigenously developed system with all major sub systems developed by DRDO laboratories and Indian industry partners. Netra Airborne Early Warning and Control System: In June 2026, DRDO handed over the Final Operational Clearance certificate for the indigenous Netra Airborne Early Warning and Control (AEW&C) system. The system was developed jointly by DRDO, the Indian Air Force, and industry partners. It significantly enhances airborne surveillance, situational awareness, and battle management capabilities. From modern combat platforms to next generation technologies, India continues to build a future ready military. These capabilities strengthen deterrence, enhance operational preparedness, and reinforce the Nation's ability to safeguard its sovereignty. Kargil's Enduring Legacy A stronger military is most meaningful when matched by unwavering resolve. Since Kargil, India has steadily strengthened both its defence capabilities and its response to evolving security challenges. This approach continues to shape the Nation's security doctrine and operational posture. Surgical Strikes and Balakot Air Strikes India's response to cross border terrorism has entered a new phase over the last decade. Following the Uri terror attack, India conducted Surgical Strikes on 28 and 29 September 2016. The operation inflicted heavy losses on terrorists and their protectors across the Line of Control. It marked a more proactive approach against cross border terrorism. A few years later, on 14 February 2019, the Pulwama terror attack claimed 40 CRPF jawans. India’s response came swiftly. On 26 February 2019, in an intelligence-led operation, the Balakot airstrikes eliminated a large number of Jaish-e-Mohammad terrorists. The facility targeted was located far from civilian areas and headed by Maulana Yousuf Azhar, brother-in-law of JeM chief Masood Azhar. These pre-emptive actions showed the world that India would no longer tolerate proxy war through terrorism. Operation SINDOOR India's evolving military doctrine was further demonstrated during Operation SINDOOR in May 2025. The operation followed the terrorist attack on civilians in Pahalgam. The Armed Forces struck nine terrorist camps in Pakistan and Pakistan occupied Jammu and Kashmir. The operation relied on accurate intelligence, drones, loitering munitions, and layered air defence. Key Jaish-e-Mohammad and Lashkar-e-Taiba command centres were destroyed. The strikes resulted in over 100 terrorists killed in action. Those eliminated included individuals linked to IC-814 hijack and Pulwama blast like Yusuf Azhar, Abdul Malik Rauf and Mudassir Ahmad. Pakistan launched drone and missile attacks on 7 and 8 May. India's integrated air defence systems intercepted them swiftly. The response showcased India's net centric warfare capabilities and integrated counter unmanned aerial systems grid. From Kargil to Operation SINDOOR, India's response to terrorism has become increasingly proactive, precise, and decisive. Celebrating the Spirit of Kargil While the legacy of Kargil continues to shape India's military resolve, it also lives on in the Nation's collective memory. Every year, Kargil Vijay Diwas brings the country together to honour the courage and sacrifice of the Bravehearts of 1999. Across the country, commemorative events are being organised to pay tribute to their supreme sacrifice. These initiatives celebrate their legacy while inspiring future generations with the values of courage, duty, and patriotism. Shaurya Vijay Yatra Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh flagged off the 13-day Shaurya Vijay Yatra on 14 July 2026. The motorcycle expedition began at the National War Memorial in New Delhi. It will conclude at the Kargil War Memorial in Dras after covering 1,900 kilometres. 28 riders, including serving and retired defence personnel with their families, are participating. The expedition carries the motto "One Ride, One Nation, One Salute." Wheels of Valour: Sanchar Shakti As part of the nationwide Wheels of Valour: Sanchar Shakti expedition, the Corps of Signals Dare Devils created a new world record on 1 July 2026. Ten riders performed on two motorcycles inside the Atal Tunnel. They completed the 9.8-kilometre tunnel in 9 minutes and 47.97 seconds. The feat honoured the spirit of Kargil Vijay Diwas while showcasing military skill, endurance, and teamwork. Tiger Hill Expedition 2026 The Indian Army and the Civil Administration, Dras, organised the Tiger Hill Expedition on 17 July 2026. The initiative promoted military tourism while preserving the legacy of the Kargil War. Eleven trained local trekking guides also participated, creating livelihood opportunities for local youth. Honouring Veterans and Bravehearts On 16 July 2026, Tri Services Ex Servicemen and their families visited the Kargil War Memorial and Heritage Hut Museum. The visit honoured the Bravehearts of Kargil and strengthened the enduring bond among veterans, serving personnel, and their families. Ex Servicemen, school children, and villagers also paid tribute at the Khalubar War Memorial on 10 July 2026. The ceremony reaffirmed the enduring values of patriotism, courage, and selfless service. Commemorative Treks and Military Displays On 13 July 2026, 137 soldiers undertook a commemorative trek to Point 5140, also known as Gun Hill. The trek honoured the Regiment of Artillery for its decisive contribution during Operation Vijay. Indian Army also organised a Weapon and Equipment Display at Hanle. The exhibition showcased modern weapons, drones, and surveillance systems. It highlighted the Indian Army's technological capabilities and operational readiness in high altitude areas. Leh to Dras Motorcycle Expedition On 12 and 13 July 2026, Indian Army riders undertook a motorcycle expedition from Leh to the Kargil War Memorial in Dras. The riders crossed the challenging Fotu La, Namika La, and Umba La passes. The expedition honoured the Bravehearts of Operation Vijay while demonstrating endurance, camaraderie, and military spirit. These commemorative events ensure that the legacy of Kargil continues to inspire every generation with the timeless ideals of courage, sacrifice, and service to the Nation. The Victory That Lives On Twenty-seven years later, the echoes of Kargil still resonate across the Nation. The victory stands as an enduring symbol of courage, sacrifice, and unwavering patriotism. Every peak recaptured reminds us that India's sovereignty is non-negotiable and will be defended at any cost. Inspired by the valour of its Bravehearts, India has emerged stronger, better prepared, and increasingly self-reliant. As the Nation salutes the heroes of Kargil, it also renews its solemn resolve to uphold their legacy. Their courage will forever inspire generations to serve the Nation with honour, duty, and unwavering commitment.
